33:60.ar: ۞لَّئِن لَّمۡ يَنتَهِ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ وَٱلۡمُرۡجِفُونَ فِي ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ لَنُغۡرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يُجَاوِرُونَكَ فِيهَآ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
33:60.en: If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the alarmists in the city do not cease, We verily shall urge thee on against them, then they will be your neighbours in it but a little while

33:61.ar: مَّلۡعُونِينَۖ أَيۡنَمَا ثُقِفُوٓاْ أُخِذُواْ وَقُتِّلُواْ تَقۡتِيلࣰ ا
33:61.en: Accursed, they will be seized wherever found and slain with a (fierce) slaughter

33:62.ar: سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ ٱللَّهِ تَبۡدِيلࣰ ا
33:62.en: That was the way of Allah in the case of those who passed away of old; thou wilt not find for the way of Allah aught of power to change

33:63.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُكَ ٱلنَّاسُ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَا يُدۡرِيكَ لَعَلَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ تَكُونُ قَرِيبًا
33:63.en: Men ask thee of the Hour. Say: The knowledge of it is with Allah only. What can convey (the knowledge) unto thee? It may be that the Hour is nigh

33:64.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمۡ سَعِيرًا
33:64.en: Lo! Allah hath cursed the disbelievers, and hath prepared for them a flaming fire

33:65.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدࣰ اۖ لَّا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيࣰّ ا وَلَا نَصِيرࣰ ا
33:65.en: Wherein they will abide for ever. They will find (then) no protecting friend nor helper

33:66.ar: يَوۡمَ تُقَلَّبُ وُجُوهُهُمۡ فِي ٱلنَّارِ يَقُولُونَ يَٰلَيۡتَنَآ أَطَعۡنَا ٱللَّهَ وَأَطَعۡنَا ٱلرَّسُولَا۠
33:66.en: On the day when their faces are turned over in the Fire, they say: Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and had obeyed His messenger

33:67.ar: وَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّآ أَطَعۡنَا سَادَتَنَا وَكُبَرَآءَنَا فَأَضَلُّونَا ٱلسَّبِيلَا۠
33:67.en: And they say: Our Lord! Lo! we obeyed our princes and great men, and they misled us from the Way

33:68.ar: رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِهِمۡ ضِعۡفَيۡنِ مِنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ وَٱلۡعَنۡهُمۡ لَعۡنࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
33:68.en: Our Lord! Oh, give them double torment and curse them with a mighty curse

33:69.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ ءَاذَوۡاْ مُوسَىٰ فَبَرَّأَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِمَّا قَالُواْۚ وَكَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَجِيهࣰ ا
33:69.en: O ye who believe! Be not as those who slandered Moses, but Allah proved his innocence of that which they alleged, and he was well esteemed in Allah's sight

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

33:13.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَٰٓأَهۡلَ يَثۡرِبَ لَا مُقَامَ لَكُمۡ فَٱرۡجِعُواْۚ وَيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُ فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلنَّبِيَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنَا عَوۡرَةࣱ وَمَا هِيَ بِعَوۡرَةٍۖ إِن يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
33:13.en: And when a party of them said: O folk of Yathrib! There is no stand (possible) for you, therefor turn back. And certain of them (even) sought permission of the Prophet, saying: Our homes lie open (to the enemy). And they lay not open. They but wished to flee

4:78.ar: أَيۡنَمَا تَكُونُواْ يُدۡرِككُّمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ وَلَوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُرُوجࣲ مُّشَيَّدَةࣲۗ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ حَسَنَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِكَۚ قُلۡ كُلࣱّ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَالِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفۡقَهُونَ حَدِيثࣰ ا
4:78.en: Wheresoever ye may be, death will overtake you, even though ye were in lofty towers. Yet if a happy thing befalleth them they say: This is from Allah; and if an evil thing befalleth them they say: This is of thy doing (O Muhammad). Say (unto them): All is from Allah. What is amiss with these people that they come not nigh to understand a happening

109:6.en: Unto you your religion, and unto me my religion

34:31.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَلَا بِٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِۗ وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ مَوۡقُوفُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ يَرۡجِعُ بَعۡضُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ يَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لَوۡلَآ أَنتُمۡ لَكُنَّا مُؤۡمِنِينَ
34:31.en: And those who disbelieve say: We believe not in this Qur'an nor in that which was before it; but oh, if thou couldst see, when the wrong-doers are brought up before their Lord, how they cast the blame one to another; how those who were despised (in the earth) say unto those who were proud: But for you, we should have been believers

34:32.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُوٓاْ أَنَحۡنُ صَدَدۡنَٰكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَكُمۖ بَلۡ كُنتُم مُّجۡرِمِينَ
34:32.en: Those who were proud say unto those who were despised: Did we drive you away from the guidance after it had come unto you? Nay, but ye were guilty

34:33.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ بَلۡ مَكۡرُ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذۡ تَأۡمُرُونَنَآ أَن نَّكۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَنَجۡعَلَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادࣰ اۚ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ فِيٓ أَعۡنَاقِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۖ هَلۡ يُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
34:33.en: Those who were despised say unto those who were proud: Nay but (it was your) scheming night and day, when ye commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals unto Him. And they are filled with remorse when they behold the doom; and We place carcans on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they requited aught save what they used to do

2:67.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُكُمۡ أَن تَذۡبَحُواْ بَقَرَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوࣰ اۖ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
2:67.en: And when Moses said unto his people: Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye sacrifice a cow, they said: Dost thou make game of us? He answered: Allah forbid that I should be among the foolish

385t4YW2PKM.speaker_note: Session 19 of his own Sunday Al-Ahzab series; one voice, shares his own experience of growing up in a culture of fear; a brief audience question near 38:30.
385t4YW2PKM.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 19: Those Who Spread Fear, the Hour, and Blaming Our Leaders (33:60-69)
385t4YW2PKM.one_line: Against mystical faith and the culture of fear: the fearmongers of Madinah, the unknown Hour, no excuse in obeying leaders, and Musa's slanderers.
385t4YW2PKM.summary: Opening the surah's finale, he argues that verses only make sense in context and that the surah's uncomfortable stories mature our faith by showing everyone as human. He criticises a mystical religiosity that avoids reality, from hiding a terminal diagnosis to imagining the Quran arrived without human effort, and calls for balance: see the Prophet's humanity, as in the date-palm incident, yet revere him above all. 33:60-62 threaten the hypocrites, the sick-hearted and those who spread fear in Madinah. He dwells on fear as a tool of oppressive politics, on Muslims' relief after the Toronto van attack instead of grief, on Middle Eastern upbringing that teaches people to keep their heads down, and on his own youth teaching children with no one's support. Courage only means something when you have something to lose; we should not fear other ideologies, and should spread hope. The Hour is known only to Allah, and a doomsday mindset that stops people trying is un-Islamic. The disbelievers cursed here are those who waged war on the Prophet, not every non-Muslim. In the Fire people wish they had obeyed and blame their chiefs, which the surah rejects: obedience is owed to Allah alone. 33:69 warns against harming the Prophet as Musa was harmed. He closes on Ibn Ata'illah: effort is itself part of destiny.

outline.heading: The finale, and why context matters
outline.gist: Familiar closing verses take on new meaning within the surah's theme; understanding why a verse is placed where it is gives the Quran its sense.

outline.heading: Verses ripped out of context
outline.gist: Using a verse as evidence without its surah usually misuses it; Al-Ahzab opens a cluster on obedience, and here on obeying when it is hardest.

outline.heading: Everyone in these stories was human
outline.gist: It is easier to imagine perfect companions and a Prophet without struggle, but working through their humanity makes faith mature.

outline.heading: Mystical faith as an escape from reality
outline.gist: Many prefer to believe a dua will make reality vanish; families even hide a terminal diagnosis from the person whose life it is.

outline.heading: The Quran did not arrive by magic
outline.gist: Learning the labour of generations and the many modes of recitation can shake a mystical faith, but understanding it makes your religion mature.

outline.heading: Holding the balance
outline.gist: See the Prophet as human with fears and mistakes yet revere him above all; likewise rely on Allah and also study for the exam.

outline.heading: The date palms: his opinion was human
outline.gist: His passing remark about pollination was taken as revelation and the harvest failed; he said you know your worldly affairs best.

outline.heading: We can only follow a human example
outline.gist: If he did not share our urges, fears and needs, we could excuse ourselves; because he did, he is our witness and example.

outline.heading: Recap: the jilbab as a hard command
outline.gist: Covering is still a struggle for many sisters and we do not blame them, but it is a command, placed in the surah of hard commands.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:60-62
outline.gist: He recites the verses with notes on assimilation and pronunciation.

outline.heading: Three groups, back to the Confederates
outline.gist: Unless they stop: the hypocrites, the sick of heart and the fearmongers, the same groups that emerged when the Confederates approached.

outline.heading: Diseased hearts exposed by life
outline.gist: Everyone has hidden defects of character; hardship exposes them unless you look inside and work on them first.

outline.heading: Al-murjifun: those who make people tremble
outline.gist: From the word for shivering; Allah would set the Prophet over them and they would not remain his neighbours for long; the third name explains what all three were doing.

outline.heading: Fear as a political tool
outline.gist: Dirty politicians and totalitarian governments spread fear because frightened people will accept anything done in its name.

outline.heading: After the Toronto van attack
outline.gist: Muslims' first reaction was relief that the attacker was not Muslim, instead of grief for the victims, a sign of how far fear has spread.

outline.heading: Fear is contagious
outline.gist: Frightened people are easy to manipulate and feel guilty for things they had nothing to do with.

outline.heading: The fearmongers at the Trench
outline.gist: They told Madinah there was no point standing firm and pleaded that their houses were exposed, discouraging everyone else.

outline.heading: Societies run on fear
outline.gist: Growing up in the Middle East he was taught to walk beside the wall and see nothing; frightened populations sit idle while their wealth is taken.

outline.heading: Teaching with no one's support
outline.gist: As a youth teaching children, no one, not even his father, supported him for fear he would be taken; at 17 he was taken to an intelligence facility.

outline.heading: Courage needs something to lose
outline.gist: Superman is not brave because nothing can hurt him; bravery exists only where there is fear.

outline.heading: Those with nothing to lose have no ethics
outline.gist: Armies try to make soldiers feel they have nothing to lose; such people, including some claiming Islam, will do anything; the companions had everything to live for and stood anyway.

outline.heading: Cursed wherever they are found
outline.gist: Those who persist in spreading fear are to be expelled or seized; verses prescribing killing are very few and specific, and fear today causes bloodshed tomorrow.

outline.heading: Fear and hatred come together
outline.gist: The culture of fear and hatred spreading in America can have no positive outcome unless it stops.

outline.heading: Do not fear other ideas
outline.gist: You only fear an ideology you think stronger than yours; he was told not to read certain books, but confidence in Islam means engaging openly, as his friend welcomes door-to-door missionaries.

outline.heading: Why the verse is at the end of the surah
outline.gist: Separated from the battle story, the rule is universal: do not spread fear, spread hope; some fear is healthy, too much paralyses.

outline.heading: Allah's sunnah that does not change
outline.gist: Those who spread fear have always been dealt with this way.

outline.heading: Caught by their own fear
outline.gist: Fearmongers are overtaken by the fear they spread; you cannot outrun death, you walk towards it.

outline.heading: No comfortable part of this surah
outline.gist: Al-Ahzab is meant to be hard; accept it and your faith will grow.

outline.heading: Question: was this a ruling for all time?
outline.gist: Expelling them was addressed to the Prophet specifically; the lesson not to tolerate fearmongering is general, and the sunnah is that they are undone by their own fear.

outline.heading: Afterwards the hypocrites held their tongues
outline.gist: By Tabuk few dared to scare the Muslims publicly, unlike at the Trench.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:63-68 and the oval mark
outline.gist: He recites the verses and explains the mark over an alif that is pronounced when stopping but dropped in continuous reading.

outline.heading: Knowledge of the Hour is with Allah alone
outline.gist: Perhaps it is near; ma yudrika points to something unknown, and the Prophet did not know its time.

outline.heading: The doomsday mentality
outline.gist: Hunting for signs of the end only makes people stop trying; we should work to postpone the Hour by reducing the ignorance and bloodshed that signal it.

outline.heading: Which disbelievers are cursed
outline.gist: Al-kafirin here means those who waged war on the Prophet, like the Confederates, not non-Muslims living peacefully with Muslims.

outline.heading: Do not yank a verse out of its surah
outline.gist: If you want a verse without context, use 'you have your religion and I have mine'; cutting verses loose kills their meaning.

outline.heading: "If only we had obeyed"
outline.gist: As faces are turned in the Fire they wish they had obeyed Allah and the Messenger: the theme of the whole cluster.

outline.heading: "We obeyed our chiefs"
outline.gist: Their excuse is that their leaders and elders led them astray, the most common human excuse.

outline.heading: Obedience is owed to Allah alone
outline.gist: If any imam, sheikh, leader or president tells you something against what you know Allah teaches, do not follow; carry your own choices.

outline.heading: "Double their punishment"
outline.gist: In their regret they ask Allah to punish their leaders more, as in other surahs of the cluster; misleaders bear their own sin and a copy of their followers'.

outline.heading: No one will carry you
outline.gist: Being misled by someone quoting the Quran is no excuse; he has no authority over you, so think for yourself.

outline.heading: The fantasy of being carried by a sheikh
outline.gist: Expecting one's spiritual master to stand with the Prophet and bring his followers through is another mystical escape; the Quran says each answers for himself.

outline.heading: Do not be like those who harmed Musa
outline.gist: Allah cleared Musa of what they said, and he was honoured in Allah's sight.

outline.heading: What Musa endured from his people
outline.gist: Accused of a physical defect for his modesty, mocked over the cow, blamed in the desert for leaving slavery; vindicated in the end.

outline.heading: The Prophet harmed in the same ways
outline.gist: Slandered over Zaynab, called a liar at the Trench, mistreated in his home; know his humanity and his status together and you will love him differently.

outline.heading: Ibn Ata'illah: resolve cannot pierce destiny
outline.gist: The third aphorism builds on the second: give 110 percent, but understand effort cannot overturn what Allah has decreed.

outline.heading: Your effort is part of destiny
outline.gist: Understanding effort as itself decreed lets you live at peace whatever happens; many young Muslims hit a wall over qadar, so he will explain it next.

outline.heading: Outro

34:22.ar: قُلِ ٱدۡعُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمۡتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا لَهُمۡ فِيهِمَا مِن شِرۡكࣲ وَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡهُم مِّن ظَهِيرࣲ‏
34:22.en: Say (O Muhammad): Call upon those whom ye set up beside Allah! They possess not an atom's weight either in the heavens or in the earth, nor have they any share in either, nor hath He an auxiliary among them

34:23.ar: وَلَا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا لِمَنۡ أَذِنَ لَهُۥۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَن قُلُوبِهِمۡ قَالُواْ مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ
34:23.en: No intercession availeth with Him save for him whom He permitteth. Yet, when fear is banished from their hearts, they say: What was it that your Lord said? They say: The Truth. And He is the Sublime, the Great

34:24.ar: ۞قُلۡ مَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۖ وَإِنَّآ أَوۡ إِيَّاكُمۡ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
34:24.en: Say: Who giveth you provision from the sky and the earth? Say: Allah, Lo! we or you assuredly are rightly guided or in error manifest

34:25.ar: قُل لَّا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّآ أَجۡرَمۡنَا وَلَا نُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
34:25.en: Say: Ye will not be asked of what we committed, nor shall we be asked of what ye do

34:26.ar: قُلۡ يَجۡمَعُ بَيۡنَنَا رَبُّنَا ثُمَّ يَفۡتَحُ بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَهُوَ ٱلۡفَتَّاحُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
34:26.en: Say: Our Lord will bring us all together, then He will judge between us with truth. He is the All-knowing Judge

34:27.ar: قُلۡ أَرُونِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَلۡحَقۡتُم بِهِۦ شُرَكَآءَۖ كَلَّاۚ بَلۡ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
34:27.en: Say: Show me those whom ye have joined unto Him as partners. Nay (ye dare not)! For He is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise

34:28.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ إِلَّا كَآفَّةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِ بَشِيرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ ا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
34:28.en: And We have not sent thee (O Muhammad) save as a bringer of good tidings and a warner unto all mankind; but most of mankind know not

34:29.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلۡوَعۡدُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
34:29.en: And they say: When is this promise (to be fulfilled) if ye are truthful

34:30.ar: قُل لَّكُم مِّيعَادُ يَوۡمࣲ لَّا تَسۡتَـٔۡخِرُونَ عَنۡهُ سَاعَةࣰ وَلَا تَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ
34:30.en: Say (O Muhammad): Yours is the promise of a Day which ye cannot postpone nor hasten by an hour

34:31.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَلَا بِٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِۗ وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ مَوۡقُوفُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ يَرۡجِعُ بَعۡضُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ يَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لَوۡلَآ أَنتُمۡ لَكُنَّا مُؤۡمِنِينَ
34:31.en: And those who disbelieve say: We believe not in this Qur'an nor in that which was before it; but oh, if thou couldst see, when the wrong-doers are brought up before their Lord, how they cast the blame one to another; how those who were despised (in the earth) say unto those who were proud: But for you, we should have been believers

34:32.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُوٓاْ أَنَحۡنُ صَدَدۡنَٰكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَكُمۖ بَلۡ كُنتُم مُّجۡرِمِينَ
34:32.en: Those who were proud say unto those who were despised: Did we drive you away from the guidance after it had come unto you? Nay, but ye were guilty

34:33.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ بَلۡ مَكۡرُ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذۡ تَأۡمُرُونَنَآ أَن نَّكۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَنَجۡعَلَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادࣰ اۚ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ فِيٓ أَعۡنَاقِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۖ هَلۡ يُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
34:33.en: Those who were despised say unto those who were proud: Nay but (it was your) scheming night and day, when ye commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals unto Him. And they are filled with remorse when they behold the doom; and We place carcans on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they requited aught save what they used to do

11:42.ar: وَهِيَ تَجۡرِي بِهِمۡ فِي مَوۡجࣲ كَٱلۡجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِي مَعۡزِلࣲ يَٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
11:42.en: And it sailed with them amid waves like mountains, and Noah cried unto his son - and he was standing aloof - O my son! Come ride with us, and be not with the disbelievers

11:43.ar: قَالَ سَـَٔاوِيٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلࣲ يَعۡصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِۚ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَۚ وَحَالَ بَيۡنَهُمَا ٱلۡمَوۡجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُغۡرَقِينَ
11:43.en: He said: I shall betake me to some mountain that will save me from the water. (Noah) said: This day there is none that saveth from the commandment of Allah save him on whom He hath had mercy. And the wave came in between them, so he was among the drowned

53:16.en: When that which shroudeth did enshroud the lote-tree

7:187.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرۡسَىٰهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّيۖ لَا يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقۡتِهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ ثَقُلَتۡ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَا تَأۡتِيكُمۡ إِلَّا بَغۡتَةࣰۗ يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنۡهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:187.en: They ask thee of the (destined) Hour, when will it come to port. Say: Knowledge thereof is with my Lord only. He alone will manifest it at its proper time. It is heavy in the heavens and the earth. It cometh not to you save unawares. They question thee as if thou couldst be well informed thereof. Say: Knowledge thereof is with Allah only, but most of mankind know not

80:34.en: On the day when a man fleeth from his brother

80:35.en: And his mother and his father

80:36.en: And his wife and his children

14:22.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمۡ وَعۡدَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَوَعَدتُّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُكُمۡۖ وَمَا كَانَ لِيَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّن سُلۡطَٰنٍ إِلَّآ أَن دَعَوۡتُكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَجَبۡتُمۡ لِيۖ فَلَا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۖ مَّآ أَنَا۠ بِمُصۡرِخِكُمۡ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُصۡرِخِيَّ إِنِّي كَفَرۡتُ بِمَآ أَشۡرَكۡتُمُونِ مِن قَبۡلُۗ إِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
14:22.en: And Satan saith, when the matter hath been decided: Lo! Allah promised you a promise of truth; and I promised you, then failed you. And I had no power over you save that I called unto you and ye obeyed me. So blame not, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can ye help me, Lo! I disbelieved in that which ye before ascribed to me. Lo! for wrong-doers is a painful doom

eDADzmf840s.title: Tafseer of Surah Saba, Session 6 (34:25-33)
eDADzmf840s.one_line: Free will and dialogue with other communities, a Prophet sent to all people, preparing for death, and the followers and leaders blaming each other on Judgment Day.
eDADzmf840s.summary: He opens on free will as the one thing a person truly owns, which is why slavery is abhorred and fathers and sons fight; parents should guide, then let children choose. Recapping the 'Say' verses, he describes the Quranic model of dialogue: be clear about differences, let outcomes show who is guided, speak of 'our mistakes' and 'your deeds', and leave judgment to Allah; conflict is justified only by oppression. Outcomes matter, so strive fully, but do not hold Allah to a worldly deal He never made. Al-Aziz leads to the Lote Tree and to knowledge as a source of happiness, and he insists Muslims should never repeat what they do not understand or follow a scholar without question, while sessions may assume shared premises. The Prophet was sent to all people, so his message belongs to everyone. Asking when the Hour comes is the wrong question; ask what you have prepared, and accept death as the one certain fact, which many avoid thinking about. The final passage shows the weakened followers and the inflated leaders blaming each other before their Lord. Each will answer alone for how he used his free will, and giving a person the unquestioned obedience due to Allah is a modern form of shirk.

outline.heading: Free will: the only thing you truly own
outline.gist: Poor or uneducated, you still hold the steering wheel of your life; that is your dignity, which is why slavery is universally condemned.

outline.heading: Why fathers and sons fight
outline.gist: A son who wants to drive his own car, even if he will crash it, is claiming his free will; conflict comes from imposing our will on others.

outline.heading: Guide your children, then let them choose
outline.gist: Controlling parents raise submissive children who turn out badly; prepare them, let them choose and be there to help, remembering that even Nuh's son refused.

outline.heading: Submission from every angle
outline.gist: The cluster examines giving up free will to Allah from every angle; Saba looks at how whole societies submit, through the contrasting stories of Dawud and Sulayman and of Saba.

outline.heading: Three uses of 'Say'
outline.gist: A run of 'Say' verses gives a public stance, lays down a dialogue, or shows how to debate an issue; context shows which.

outline.heading: Clear differences make coexistence healthier
outline.gist: State plainly where you differ on belief, not to stoke fear but to admit difference; groups living by different beliefs and codes is acceptable.

outline.heading: Either we or you: outcomes will judge
outline.gist: Muslims do not claim to be right without evidence; strong communities, care for the weak, education and low corruption will show who is guided.

outline.heading: Our mistakes, your deeds
outline.gist: The verse calls our own conduct crimes and theirs merely deeds; all the Prophet fought for was the freedom to speak and for people to choose.

outline.heading: Strive for success, then leave results to Allah
outline.gist: Destiny is no invitation to fail: plan and exhaust every means, and if it still does not work out, rest assured it is in Allah's hands.

outline.heading: Do not hold Allah to a deal He never made
outline.gist: Failed expectations crush people into depression or addiction; Allah promised paradise for effort, not a particular worldly outcome.

outline.heading: Our Lord will judge between us
outline.gist: This is our dialogue with non-Muslim communities: a competition in success, not a clash of civilisations, unless there is clear oppression; this is the Quran's view, not a Canadian accommodation.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verses 27 to 30 and explains the six-count and four-count prolongations.

outline.heading: Show me those you added to Him
outline.gist: Alhaqtum means squeezing extra members into a group; show what they created or gave life or purpose to, or stop claiming them.

outline.heading: Al-Aziz al-Hakim: beyond reach yet wise
outline.gist: Questions about how He is beyond time and space have no answers, but because He is wise nothing is random or unrewarded.

outline.heading: The Lote Tree beyond description
outline.gist: A university friend abandoned a thesis on Sidrat al-Muntaha after three weeks; even the most eloquent Prophet could not describe what covered it.

outline.heading: Knowledge brings happiness
outline.gist: In paradise he wants history explained from Allah's perspective; understanding things, even trivial ones, satisfies, and not understanding frustrates.

outline.heading: Social knowledge and men who avoid home
outline.gist: Men who do not understand the dynamics with their wives and children feel lost at home and flee to friends where they know what to do.

outline.heading: Never repeat what you do not understand
outline.gist: People recite Juz Amma for decades without knowing its words; the companions questioned the Prophet and each other because the Quran taught them to.

outline.heading: Passive acceptance is recent
outline.gist: Only in the last two centuries have Muslims accepted whatever they hear; it serves the sheikh, not the long-term interest of the ummah.

outline.heading: Question: understanding versus acceptance
outline.gist: The basics must rest on understanding; the best explanation need not explain everything, like finding a deserted city on another planet.

outline.heading: Where to look for faith
outline.gist: Look at the universe, at life, at history and within yourself; once the basics are established you submit to Allah even where details are unclear.

outline.heading: Question me: I am just a guy
outline.gist: What a speaker says about Allah may be mistaken or biased, and he cannot carry anything for you on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Gatherings with shared premises
outline.gist: Not every gathering is a debate on God's existence; specialised groups work from agreed premises, so raise yours in the right setting.

outline.heading: Question: those who reject hadith
outline.gist: Answering a question, he calls it a specialised debate; the Prophet did not live 63 years silent, and the highly contextual Quran cannot be understood without his life, though the weight given to hadith is open to discussion.

outline.heading: Sent to all people
outline.gist: Kaffah means sufficing everyone; the Prophet brings good news to those who believe and warning to those who do not.

outline.heading: Muslims as bearers of good news and warning
outline.gist: Muslims identify good and harmful paths and point them out to people, in matters of this world as well as the next.

outline.heading: The message belongs to everyone
outline.gist: Most people do not know this, but Muslims must; the Prophet's teaching is the property of all humanity and everyone deserves access to it.

outline.heading: When is this promise? The wrong question
outline.gist: Humans always ask when; the Prophet did not know either, and only Allah knows the Hour.

outline.heading: What have you prepared for it?
outline.gist: Asked when the Hour would come, the Prophet asked what the man had prepared; death is your personal day of reckoning.

outline.heading: The only fact we know, and avoid
outline.gist: Our era never speaks of death; you know nothing of your future except that you will die, yet it is what we prepare for least.

outline.heading: How people die
outline.gist: As a physician and in dawah work he has seen people die ready and others terrified, and some non-Muslims better prepared than Muslims who never thought about it.

outline.heading: Death is never celebrated
outline.gist: Death ends the chance to redeem yourself; we should want long life to do better, not out of fear.

outline.heading: An appointment you cannot miss
outline.gist: You cannot delay or advance it by an hour, take a sick day or slip off the records; just know you will be there.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verse 31.

outline.heading: We will never believe in this Quran
outline.gist: They reject the Quran and all earlier scripture; the dialogue is not meant to convert everyone but to set the terms of coexistence.

outline.heading: A new section in mid-verse
outline.gist: The section on the Day of Judgment begins in the middle of a verse, so you cannot stop and must read on.

outline.heading: Wrongdoers held before their Lord
outline.gist: Tolerance in this world does not mean there is no right and wrong; the oppressors stand detained, murmuring to one another.

outline.heading: The ones made weak
outline.gist: Mustad'af means made weak, often by your own choice: someone who wasted his youth on games has no opinion of his own and adopts whoever's view he hears.

outline.heading: The inflated ones: if not for you
outline.gist: Mustakbir here means those blown out of proportion; the followers blame leaders they never met for poisoning their minds.

outline.heading: You alone are accountable
outline.gist: Parents, teachers and peer pressure will not carry it; doing something you cannot make sense of because a person said so is wrong even if it happens to be right.

outline.heading: Never 'because I said so'
outline.gist: Free will is surrendered to Allah alone; parents should explain rather than demand blind obedience, since that child will one day be wiser than them.

outline.heading: Did you do it? Raising responsible children
outline.gist: Focus on what the child did, not who provoked him; the Day of Judgment will ask only that, so own it, defend it, or stop and repent.

outline.heading: Why people flee their families that Day
outline.gist: He reads the flight from mother and son as fear of being blamed, as companions in wrongdoing avoid each other's eyes.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verses 32 and 33.

outline.heading: Did we hold you back?
outline.gist: The leaders answer that they never forced anyone; the followers clapped and nodded, and no tyrant like Pharaoh can rule without supporters.

outline.heading: Iblis's own sermon
outline.gist: Iblis will likewise say he only called and they answered, so blame yourselves.

outline.heading: Plotting night and day
outline.gist: The followers reply that the leaders schemed day and night to manipulate how they thought; now that everything is clear they see they were played.

outline.heading: Setting up equals today
outline.gist: No one worships rocks now; shirk takes the form of accepting people, ideologies or sources without question the way only Allah's word should be accepted.

outline.heading: Hidden regret and chains
outline.gist: Seeing the punishment, both sides hide their regret; chains go on the necks of all, and each is repaid only for what he did.

outline.heading: No one will pay your bill
outline.gist: Listen to advice but question everything; whoever pays the bill should order what he wants, because no one will carry it for you.

34:31.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَلَا بِٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِۗ وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ مَوۡقُوفُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ يَرۡجِعُ بَعۡضُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ يَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لَوۡلَآ أَنتُمۡ لَكُنَّا مُؤۡمِنِينَ
34:31.en: And those who disbelieve say: We believe not in this Qur'an nor in that which was before it; but oh, if thou couldst see, when the wrong-doers are brought up before their Lord, how they cast the blame one to another; how those who were despised (in the earth) say unto those who were proud: But for you, we should have been believers

34:32.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُوٓاْ أَنَحۡنُ صَدَدۡنَٰكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَكُمۖ بَلۡ كُنتُم مُّجۡرِمِينَ
34:32.en: Those who were proud say unto those who were despised: Did we drive you away from the guidance after it had come unto you? Nay, but ye were guilty

34:33.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ بَلۡ مَكۡرُ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذۡ تَأۡمُرُونَنَآ أَن نَّكۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَنَجۡعَلَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادࣰ اۚ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ فِيٓ أَعۡنَاقِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۖ هَلۡ يُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
34:33.en: Those who were despised say unto those who were proud: Nay but (it was your) scheming night and day, when ye commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals unto Him. And they are filled with remorse when they behold the doom; and We place carcans on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they requited aught save what they used to do

34:34.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا فِي قَرۡيَةࣲ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتۡرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلۡتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
34:34.en: And We sent not unto any township a warner, but its pampered ones declared: Lo! we are disbelievers in that wherewith ye have been sent

34:35.ar: وَقَالُواْ نَحۡنُ أَكۡثَرُ أَمۡوَٰلࣰ ا وَأَوۡلَٰدࣰ ا وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
34:35.en: And they say: We are more (than you) in wealth and children. We are not the punished

34:36.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
34:36.en: Say (O Muhammad): Lo! my Lord enlargeth the provision for whom He will and narroweth it (for whom He will). But most of mankind know not

34:37.ar: وَمَآ أَمۡوَٰلُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُكُم بِٱلَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمۡ عِندَنَا زُلۡفَىٰٓ إِلَّا مَنۡ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ جَزَآءُ ٱلضِّعۡفِ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ وَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡغُرُفَٰتِ ءَامِنُونَ
34:37.en: And it is not your wealth nor your children that will bring you near unto Us, but he who believeth and doeth good (he draweth near). As for such, theirs will be twofold reward for what they did and they will dwell secure in lofty halls

34:39.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُ لَهُۥۚ وَمَآ أَنفَقۡتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَهُوَ يُخۡلِفُهُۥۖ وَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
34:39.en: Say: Lo! my Lord enlargeth the provision for whom He will of His bondmen, and narroweth (it) for him. And whatsoever ye spend (for good) He replaceth it. And He is the Best of Providers

34:24.ar: ۞قُلۡ مَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۖ وَإِنَّآ أَوۡ إِيَّاكُمۡ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
34:24.en: Say: Who giveth you provision from the sky and the earth? Say: Allah, Lo! we or you assuredly are rightly guided or in error manifest

34:25.ar: قُل لَّا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّآ أَجۡرَمۡنَا وَلَا نُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
34:25.en: Say: Ye will not be asked of what we committed, nor shall we be asked of what ye do

34:28.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ إِلَّا كَآفَّةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِ بَشِيرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ ا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
34:28.en: And We have not sent thee (O Muhammad) save as a bringer of good tidings and a warner unto all mankind; but most of mankind know not

34:38.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡعَوۡنَ فِيٓ ءَايَٰتِنَا مُعَٰجِزِينَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ مُحۡضَرُونَ
34:38.en: And as for those who strive against Our revelations, challenging, they will be brought to the doom

5:101.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَسۡـَٔلُواْ عَنۡ أَشۡيَآءَ إِن تُبۡدَ لَكُمۡ تَسُؤۡكُمۡ وَإِن تَسۡـَٔلُواْ عَنۡهَا حِينَ يُنَزَّلُ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ تُبۡدَ لَكُمۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
5:101.en: O ye who believe! Ask not of things which, if they were made unto you, would trouble you; but if ye ask of them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made known unto you. Allah pardoneth this, for Allah is Forgiving, Clement

12:96.ar: فَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَ ٱلۡبَشِيرُ أَلۡقَىٰهُ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ فَٱرۡتَدَّ بَصِيرࣰ اۖ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
12:96.en: Then, when the bearer of glad tidings came, he laid it on his face and he became a seer once more. He said: Said I not unto you that I know from Allah that which ye know not

7:75.ar: قَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِمَنۡ ءَامَنَ مِنۡهُمۡ أَتَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مُّرۡسَلࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦۚ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلَ بِهِۦ مُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:75.en: The chieftains of his people, who were scornful, said unto those whom they despised, unto such of them as believed: Know ye that Salih is one sent from his Lord? They said: Lo! In that wherewith he hath been sent we are believers

7:76.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِٱلَّذِيٓ ءَامَنتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
7:76.en: Those who were scornful said: Lo! in that which ye believe we are disbelievers

wghpVRY6b8E.title: Tafseer of Surah Saba, Session 7 (34:31-37)
wghpVRY6b8E.one_line: Submit to Allah alone and question everyone else; why the wealthy reject every messenger; provision is no sign of Allah's love; righteous deeds as serving your purpose.
wghpVRY6b8E.summary: Saying we submit is a claim we spend our lives proving. Recapping the scene of followers and leaders blaming each other, he argues that the greatest obstacle to a society's submission is corrupt leadership plus a submissive population. Muslims submit unconditionally to Allah alone and question everyone else, which is how the Prophet could trust young companions like Mus'ab and how Abu Bakr asked to be corrected. Questioning is tiring but keeps speakers careful and builds responsible, mature communities; the deen belongs to every attendee as much as to the imam. With young people, win by logic, not power, and focus on what matters, not haircuts. The new section explains why societies refuse: every warner was rejected first by the affluent, whose wealth lets them avoid hard questions and whose interests, like the Quraysh's and Abu Lahab's, depend on the status quo. He extends this to modern politics, where the wealthy block change, the poor's issues are ignored, and rigged systems historically produced slavery. The wealthy claim their money and status prove Allah favours them; the answer is that provision is spread or tightened by His will alone, and never a measure of His love. Only belief and righteous deeds, meaning fulfilling the purpose you were created for, bring you near, and privilege raises the bar.

outline.heading: Submission is a claim to be proven
outline.gist: When you say iyyaka na'budu, Allah says this is between Me and My servant: a claim you spend the rest of your life proving.

outline.heading: Islam means submission, not peace
outline.gist: Islam is submitting your free will, the only thing you truly own, to Allah's will, a decision with many layers.

outline.heading: Recap: the cluster and Saba's two societies
outline.gist: The first surah treated submission when it is hardest; Saba treats it at the level of societies through Dawud and Sulayman's kingdom and the people of Saba.

outline.heading: Recap: the dialogue with other communities
outline.gist: Muslim beliefs are proven by outcomes and conduct, not statements; each side answers for its own deeds.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recap: no us and them
outline.gist: The Prophet was sent to all people; the only ownership we have over his message is how deeply we follow it, and it must reach every doorstep.

outline.heading: Recap: the weak and the inflated argue
outline.gist: People are made weak by societies and accept it; others are blown out of proportion; on that Day the followers blame the leaders, who say they never held anyone back, and the followers reply that they schemed night and day.

outline.heading: Hidden regret and chains
outline.gist: Seeing the punishment ends the argument; they hide their regret and each is repaid only for what he did.

outline.heading: Every surah has a snapshot of Judgment Day
outline.gist: No surah narrates the whole Day, but almost every one has a scene tied to its theme; this one concerns how societies submit.

outline.heading: Corrupt leaders and submissive followers
outline.gist: The biggest obstacle to a society's submission is corrupt leadership combined with a submissive population; accept Allah's word without conditions and no one else's.

outline.heading: Why the Prophet could trust the young
outline.gist: Muslim youth became independent early; the Prophet relied on people in their teens and twenties, sending Mus'ab at about 21 to represent him in Madinah.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr: correct me if I err
outline.gist: On taking office Abu Bakr asked to be obeyed only while he followed the truth, and the people truly lived by it.

outline.heading: Knowledge is a tool, not a rank
outline.gist: Knowledge itself does not raise you; it is a responsibility to teach for the speaker and to think and question for the listener, who carries his decision alone.

outline.heading: Questioning keeps the speaker honest
outline.gist: Many religious figures would dislike this, but once people stop questioning, the speaker stops caring whether what he says is fully right.

outline.heading: The price is worth paying
outline.gist: Open questioning brings arguments from the ignorant, but it builds critical thinkers and a more intelligent, responsible society.

outline.heading: Owners, not employees, of the deen
outline.gist: If the deen is the imam's project, people behave like employees who are glad when the office burns; ownership changes that.

outline.heading: Passivity is also a choice
outline.gist: Choices are sacred and recorded; the imam has no more ownership of or responsibility for Islam than you, and feeling otherwise is where change must start.

outline.heading: When random questions had to be limited
outline.gist: Questions were so free in the Prophet's gatherings that random ones were eventually restricted, which is why companions welcomed Bedouins who did not know the rule.

outline.heading: Women asking whether the revelation cared about them
outline.gist: Women openly asked whether Allah addressed women at all, and the Prophet answered without rebuke: nothing was taboo.

outline.heading: Without critical thinking both sides are harmed
outline.gist: When followers do not question, the leader goes astray too; the Judgment Day argument is the result.

outline.heading: Win young people by logic
outline.gist: He works well with youth because nothing is off limits and nothing is 'because I said so'; the pure human mind respects a better argument.

outline.heading: Power teaches might makes right
outline.gist: Making children obey because you are older, stronger or pay for their food teaches them the world runs on power, not reason, against what the Quran teaches.

outline.heading: The haircut request
outline.gist: Parents' most common request is to talk to their son about his haircut; they lack an argument, and one father fixated on the haircut while his son was using marijuana daily.

outline.heading: Obedient appearance or a heart of gold
outline.gist: We prefer a son who looks and acts right in public but hates his father to a loud questioner who loves Allah; care about content over appearance.

outline.heading: Look things up and keep speakers on their toes
outline.gist: Read, search and ask until it makes sense, so speakers think before they speak and do not reshape the deen to personal interest.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verse 34 to begin the new section.

outline.heading: Why warners come first
outline.gist: Avoiding punishment matters more than gaining reward, so prophets are called warners; bashir appears alone only for the one who brought good news to Yaqub.

outline.heading: The affluent: those with more than they need
outline.gist: Mutrafuha are those with surplus; with ample wealth you can cruise through life without ever asking why you exist.

outline.heading: Hardship makes you think; wealth switches it off
outline.gist: A serious illness or near-death moment starts the questions; money lets you turn them off, so the affluent always reject the messenger.

outline.heading: Why Quraysh refused: money and authority
outline.gist: As descendants of Ibrahim they had every reason to accept, but idols at the Ka'bah secured their authority over Arabia and protected their trade.

outline.heading: Superstition that serves someone
outline.gist: Hardly anyone ever believed a rock could do anything; such beliefs persist because someone benefits from the authority they give.

outline.heading: Abu Lahab: just the money
outline.gist: The Prophet's own uncle, who raised him and knew his honesty, opposed him alone among Banu Hashim to protect the business empire he had built.

outline.heading: The wealthy resist every good idea
outline.gist: If the system works for you, even without knowing why, you will not want it changed.

outline.heading: Presidents who cannot change anything
outline.gist: Every new leader learns who really runs things; promises to tax the wealthy never happen and public debate shifts to narrower controversies.

outline.heading: The poor's issues do not pay
outline.gist: Starvation, unjust imprisonment and daily atrocities stay off the news because caring for the poor earns nothing; question what you are shown.

outline.heading: Whatever you brought, we reject
outline.gist: The affluent reject the message before hearing its content, as the arrogant among Salih's people rejected whatever the believers believed in.

outline.heading: More wealth and children means Allah loves us
outline.gist: Wealth is financial status and children social status; the affluent conclude their abundance proves they are right and will not be punished.

outline.heading: The same mentality today
outline.gist: The strongest country in the world may not say it aloud, but acts as if its wealth means its opinion and vote weigh more.

outline.heading: Rigged systems destroy societies
outline.gist: A society whose system protects the wealthy and keeps the poor at risk heads toward destruction or the enslavement of the poor.

outline.heading: How slavery begins
outline.gist: Wealthy groups build systems to grow richer; poverty brings ignorance and lost status until the poor can be treated however others wish, a pattern found on every continent.

outline.heading: Question: what does Islamic finance look like?
outline.gist: There is no detailed Islamic blueprint for the global economy, only four or five principles; any system that keeps them, such as not loading all risk on the poor, is Islamic.

outline.heading: Provision is spread or tightened by His will
outline.gist: Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it; it has nothing to do with a person's worth, so wealth is no reason to refuse a message.

outline.heading: A lesson for rich and poor alike
outline.gist: Most people do not know this; it should shape how both the wealthy and the poor understand their situation.

outline.heading: Recap of the section so far
outline.gist: The affluent reject without hearing, citing their wealth as proof; the answer is that provision depends on Allah's will alone.

outline.heading: Never measure your relationship with Allah by wealth
outline.gist: Most of us have taken a windfall as Allah's pleasure or a failed deal as His punishment; wealth moves like the tide, and living comfortably in this country can hide that.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verses 37 to 39 and points out the extra words in verse 39 compared with verse 36.

outline.heading: Wealth and children do not bring you near
outline.gist: Neither financial nor social status draws you closer to Allah in importance or pleasure; we never know the reasons for His will.

outline.heading: Amal salih: doing what you were made for
outline.gist: A phone is salih if it makes calls and a classic car only if it drives; righteous deeds are those that fulfil the purpose Allah created you for.

outline.heading: Purpose depends on who you are
outline.gist: The phrase is left open because your talents, place, age and circumstances define how you serve your purpose; a smile is good but may not be your job.

outline.heading: Wealth helps only when used for that purpose
outline.gist: Sitting in a mansion surrounded by children is no proof Allah is pleased with you unless you used it all to serve your purpose.

outline.heading: Who told you that you are a good person?
outline.gist: Answering a question, he calls 'I am good because I harm no one' arrogant: only Allah judges who is good, and by His criteria, not a bar we set ourselves.

outline.heading: More given, more expected
outline.gist: Someone born Muslim and taught the Quran will be asked about more than a new convert; privilege tempts us to lower the bar so our conscience stays clean.

outline.heading: Double reward in the high chambers
outline.gist: Those who believe and fulfil their purpose with what they were given get a twofold reward and dwell safely in the high rooms of paradise.

Never read your wealth or poverty as a sign of how Allah sees you
Find your purpose and use your wealth and status to fulfil it

33:51.ar: ۞تُرۡجِي مَن تَشَآءُ مِنۡهُنَّ وَتُـٔۡوِيٓ إِلَيۡكَ مَن تَشَآءُۖ وَمَنِ ٱبۡتَغَيۡتَ مِمَّنۡ عَزَلۡتَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكَۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَن تَقَرَّ أَعۡيُنُهُنَّ وَلَا يَحۡزَنَّ وَيَرۡضَيۡنَ بِمَآ ءَاتَيۡتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَلِيمࣰ ا
33:51.en: Thou canst defer whom thou wilt of them and receive unto thee whom thou wilt, and whomsoever thou desirest of those whom thou hast set aside (temporarily), it is no sin for thee (to receive her again); that is better; that they may be comforted and not grieve, and may all be pleased with what thou givest them. Allah knoweth what is in your hearts (O men), and Allah is ever Forgiving, Clement

33:52.ar: لَّا يَحِلُّ لَكَ ٱلنِّسَآءُ مِنۢ بَعۡدُ وَلَآ أَن تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣲ وَلَوۡ أَعۡجَبَكَ حُسۡنُهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتۡ يَمِينُكَۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ رَّقِيبࣰ ا
33:52.en: It is not allowed thee to take (other) women henceforth, nor that thou shouldst change them for other wives even though their beauty pleased thee, save those whom thy right hand possesseth. And Allah is ever Watcher over all things

33:53.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَدۡخُلُواْ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤۡذَنَ لَكُمۡ إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيۡرَ نَٰظِرِينَ إِنَىٰهُ وَلَٰكِنۡ إِذَا دُعِيتُمۡ فَٱدۡخُلُواْ فَإِذَا طَعِمۡتُمۡ فَٱنتَشِرُواْ وَلَا مُسۡتَـٔۡنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمۡ كَانَ يُؤۡذِي ٱلنَّبِيَّ فَيَسۡتَحۡيِۦ مِنكُمۡۖ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَسۡتَحۡيِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ وَإِذَا سَأَلۡتُمُوهُنَّ مَتَٰعࣰ ا فَسۡـَٔلُوهُنَّ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابࣲۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَطۡهَرُ لِقُلُوبِكُمۡ وَقُلُوبِهِنَّۚ وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمۡ أَن تُؤۡذُواْ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَآ أَن تَنكِحُوٓاْ أَزۡوَٰجَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦٓ أَبَدًاۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمۡ كَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمًا
33:53.en: O Ye who believe! Enter not the dwellings of the Prophet for a meal without waiting for the proper time, unless permission be granted you. But if ye are invited, enter, and, when your meal is ended, then disperse. Linger not for conversation. Lo! that would cause annoyance to the Prophet, and he would be shy of (asking) you (to go); but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when ye ask of them (the wives of the Prophet) anything, ask it of them from behind a curtain. That is purer for your hearts and for their hearts. And it is not for you to cause annoyance to the messenger of Allah, nor that ye should ever marry his wives after him. Lo! that in Allah's sight would be an enormity

33:54.ar: إِن تُبۡدُواْ شَيۡـًٔا أَوۡ تُخۡفُوهُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣰ ا
33:54.en: Whether ye divulge a thing or keep it hidden, lo! Allah is ever Knower of all things

33:55.ar: لَّا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِنَّ فِيٓ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ وَلَآ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ وَلَآ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ وَلَآ أَبۡنَآءِ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ وَلَآ أَبۡنَآءِ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ وَلَا نِسَآئِهِنَّ وَلَا مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّۗ وَٱتَّقِينَ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدًا
33:55.en: It is no sin for them (thy wives) to converse freely) with their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their brothers' sons, or the sons of their sisters or of their own women, or their slaves. O women! Keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is ever Witness over all things

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

33:50.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِنَّآ أَحۡلَلۡنَا لَكَ أَزۡوَٰجَكَ ٱلَّٰتِيٓ ءَاتَيۡتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ يَمِينُكَ مِمَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمِّكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمَّٰتِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَٰلَٰتِكَ ٱلَّٰتِي هَاجَرۡنَ مَعَكَ وَٱمۡرَأَةࣰ مُّؤۡمِنَةً إِن وَهَبَتۡ نَفۡسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنۡ أَرَادَ ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَن يَسۡتَنكِحَهَا خَالِصَةࣰ لَّكَ مِن دُونِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَۗ قَدۡ عَلِمۡنَا مَا فَرَضۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِهِمۡ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ لِكَيۡلَا يَكُونَ عَلَيۡكَ حَرَجࣱۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
33:50.en: O Prophet! Lo! We have made lawful unto thee thy wives unto whom thou hast paid their dowries, and those whom thy right hand possesseth of those whom Allah hath given thee as spoils of war, and the daughters of thine uncle on the father's side and the daughters of thine aunts on the father's side, and the daughters of thine uncle on the mother's side and the daughters of thine aunts on the mother's side who emigrated with thee, and a believing woman if she give herself unto the Prophet and the Prophet desire to ask her in marriage - a privilege for thee only, not for the (rest of) believers - We are Aware of that which We enjoined upon them concerning their wives and those whom their right hands possess - that thou mayst be free from blame, for Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled

2:26.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسۡتَحۡيِۦٓ أَن يَضۡرِبَ مَثَلࣰ ا مَّا بَعُوضَةࣰ فَمَا فَوۡقَهَاۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلࣰ اۘ يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَيَهۡدِي بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ اۚ وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
2:26.en: Lo! Allah disdaineth not to coin the similitude even of a gnat. Those who believe know that it is the truth from their Lord; but those who disbelieve say: What doth Allah wish (to teach) by such a similitude? He misleadeth many thereby, and He guideth many thereby; and He misleadeth thereby only miscreants

33:38.ar: مَّا كَانَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲ فِيمَا فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥۖ سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلُۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ قَدَرࣰ ا مَّقۡدُورًا
33:38.en: There is no reproach for the Prophet in that which Allah maketh his due. That was Allah's way with those who passed away of old - and the commandment of Allah is certain destiny

33:33.ar: وَقَرۡنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ وَأَقِمۡنَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتِينَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِعۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ تَطۡهِيرࣰ ا
33:33.en: And stay in your houses. Bedizen not yourselves with the bedizenment of the Time of Ignorance. Be regular in prayer, and pay the poor-due, and obey Allah and His messenger. Allah's wish is but to remove uncleanness far from you, O Folk of the Household, and cleanse you with a thorough cleansing

eStq3_vYNzA.speaker_note: Session 17 of his own Sunday Al-Ahzab series; one voice, recalls his own student days visiting scholars.
eStq3_vYNzA.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 17: Fairness Among His Wives and the Etiquette of His Home (33:51-55)
eStq3_vYNzA.one_line: The Prophet's freedom in dividing time among his wives, the end of new marriages, and the manners and screen required in his home.
eStq3_vYNzA.summary: Continuing the rulings specific to the Prophet, he explains 33:51: Allah let him choose which wives to draw near or set aside, so that whatever he gave would be received as a gift and not demanded as a right, yet he still divided his nights equally. Allah knows what is in hearts, and as All-Knowing and Forbearing He did not punish those who doubted him. He contrasts the strict financial conditions on other men with multiple wives, and notes the Prophet never divorced a wife. In 33:52, revealed alongside the permissions, he is forbidden to marry again or exchange wives, which shows the surah's point: Allah makes lawful and unlawful as He wills and believers accept both. The next chapter enters his house. People overstayed for hours and he was too polite to object, so 33:53 limits entry to invitations for food and asks guests to leave after eating; Allah is not shy of the truth. He distinguishes haya from mere embarrassment, applies the lesson to how students treat scholars' time, and explains the extra screen for the wives in casual conversation, purer for all hearts since no one could marry them after him. He draws a lesson on unnecessary familiarity with the opposite gender at work and ends with a brief note from Ibn Ata'illah on resolve and destiny.

outline.heading: Recap: obedience when it is hard
outline.gist: Obeying Allah is what the deen is built on; points count most when obedience is difficult.

outline.heading: Recap of the surah's chapters so far
outline.gist: The Trench, the wives' choice, women in the deen, the Zaynab marriage, dhikr as the remedy, and the verses on his status.

outline.heading: Accepting that he is treated differently
outline.gist: Accepting rulings unique to him, including options he never used, is part of accepting the deen under 33:36.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:51 and counting the madd
outline.gist: He recites the verse, pointing out twelve counts of elongation in one short phrase.

outline.heading: Defer whom you will, draw near whom you will
outline.gist: The two verbs mean pushing away and bringing close: from the women made lawful in 33:50 he could marry or not as he chose.

outline.heading: Those you set aside: time among his wives
outline.gist: The second part concerns wives he spent less time with; he may return to any of them without blame.

outline.heading: He chose equal division anyway
outline.gist: Though not obliged, he gave every wife her night, except Sawdah, who in old age gave hers away.

outline.heading: Why the ruling: contentment
outline.gist: When something is not your right, whatever you receive is a gift; that is how their eyes would be cooled, without grief and with acceptance.

outline.heading: Allah knows what is in your hearts
outline.gist: The surah repeatedly speaks to inner psychology; these verses exist so no one has grounds to question his conduct.

outline.heading: Conditions on other men who marry again
outline.gist: A man may not halve his first wife's provision to marry again but must afford equal homes and support; the Prophet had no wealth at all.

outline.heading: His character with his wives
outline.gist: He did not seek out particular women or ages, did not mistreat his wives, and there is no reliable report he ever divorced one.

outline.heading: All-Knowing and Wise
outline.gist: You trust a command when the one giving it knows everything and is wise; that pairing is common in the Quran.

outline.heading: All-Knowing and Forbearing
outline.gist: A saying: I would rather Allah judge me than my parents, since a mother who learned all your secrets might lose her compassion; Allah knows all and stays forbearing.

outline.heading: Hilm as a branch of sabr
outline.gist: Sabr is the umbrella; hilm is not reacting harshly to what would provoke it, so Allah did not punish those who doubted the Prophet.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:52
outline.gist: He recites the next verse.

outline.heading: No more wives, and no exchanging
outline.gist: From then on he could neither marry new women nor divorce one to replace her, however impressed by someone's excellence.

outline.heading: Milk al-yamin is also a contract
outline.gist: Marriage to a woman not free is a contract with different conditions, such as half the dowry and half the penalty, not unrestricted possession.

outline.heading: Did he have a concubine?
outline.gist: There is no authentic report that he did; Mariyah's status is narrated both ways.

outline.heading: Allah is watching over everything
outline.gist: Raqib is the one who observes and regulates, like a regulatory body in Middle Eastern governments.

outline.heading: Permitted and forbidden in the same breath
outline.gist: These verses came close together, around year six or seven, showing that the point is what Allah makes lawful or not.

outline.heading: A verse no author would write for himself
outline.gist: An orientalist was puzzled why the Prophet would include a verse forbidding himself; it serves only the message of submission.

outline.heading: His wives at that time, and Mariyah's timeline
outline.gist: He lists the wives then living; Mariyah was a gift from the ruler of Egypt, and her marriage cannot be dated against this verse.

outline.heading: A new chapter: visitors in his home
outline.gist: Picture living in Madinah: how often would you try to sit with him? People knocked all day, five minutes became three hours.

outline.heading: Do not hold scholars to his standard
outline.gist: He never showed annoyance; hold yourself to his standard, but do not expect it of every scholar you visit.

outline.heading: Guests who would not leave
outline.gist: Visitors stayed for hours, were fed, and stayed again, daily, just to chat.

outline.heading: Al-A'mash and the heavy-blooded guest
outline.gist: A man visiting the sick al-A'mash asked if he was a burden and was told he was a burden even at home; scholars wrote whole books on such people.

outline.heading: A teacher, leader and family man
outline.gist: People travelled great distances to see him while others simply had nothing to do; he also had duties to his wives and children.

outline.heading: His large household
outline.gist: His wives' children from earlier marriages, Khadijah's children, Zayd and Ali all lived with him, then grandchildren too.

outline.heading: Umar's concern and the word hijab
outline.gist: Unknown men came in and out constantly; Umar asked that the wives be screened, and here alone the Quran uses the word hijab.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:53, first part
outline.gist: He recites the opening of the verse.

outline.heading: Enter only with permission, for food
outline.gist: Meet him elsewhere to talk; enter his home only when invited and for a meal, though he loved feeding the poor; close family and advisers were exempt.

outline.heading: Eat, then leave
outline.gist: Do not wait in his house while food is prepared or linger afterwards seeking conversation.

outline.heading: Allah is not shy of the truth
outline.gist: The Prophet was too shy to tell them, but Allah is not; the surah gradually trains us to lose shame about His commands and the opinions of people.

outline.heading: Years of patience before the verse
outline.gist: For perhaps four years he endured guests lingering hours after food without a word.

outline.heading: Haya versus embarrassment
outline.gist: Haya is refusing to do what is beneath you because you would not want Allah to see it; khajal is just being flustered; in 2:26 Allah is not shy to give an example.

outline.heading: How awkward this was to recite
outline.gist: Having learned to feel no distress at commands, he still had to recite a verse that made regular visitors shrink in their clothes.

outline.heading: The parallel for scholars today
outline.gist: As students they were reminded of this verse when visiting scholars: stay only as long as you need, since they too are human and too polite to say so.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:53-55 and its many madd
outline.gist: He recites the rest, counting the elongations and nasal sounds.

outline.heading: Asking his wives for everyday things
outline.gist: Mata' means ordinary worldly matters with no religious purpose, like asking for lentils or salt.

outline.heading: Speaking to the opposite gender is permitted
outline.gist: Courteous, professional conversation at work or in an elevator is normal, provided the conduct code of earlier verses is kept.

outline.heading: An extra screen for his wives
outline.gist: Beyond the dress code all Muslim women keep, his wives were to be spoken to from behind a barrier in casual matters, given how many men passed through.

outline.heading: Purer for your hearts and theirs
outline.gist: Some men thought of marrying a wife of his after his death, and daily contact could nurture that.

outline.heading: Never harm him or marry his wives after him
outline.gist: Idle daily conversation with his wives harmed him, and marrying them after him would be enormous in Allah's sight.

outline.heading: Whether you reveal or conceal it
outline.gist: Allah knows what some companions thought; they were human.

outline.heading: The screen was for casual talk, not religion
outline.gist: Aisha led an army and spoke to men face to face, fully covered, about prayer, Uthman's killing and the Quran; the screen applied only to idle matters.

outline.heading: The Quran speaks indirectly here
outline.gist: The verse hints that thoughts existed without naming them.

outline.heading: A lesson for our own conduct
outline.gist: If the companions needed this, so do we: keep dealings with the opposite gender purposeful and professional, especially when married, through how you face and speak to people.

outline.heading: Relatives exempt from the screen
outline.gist: No blame on the wives before fathers, sons, brothers, nephews, women and those they own.

outline.heading: Fear Allah, the Witness of all
outline.gist: Imagine the companions hearing these rulings on his home and wives; they changed social life and were hard; the next chapter is lighter.

outline.heading: Ibn Ata'illah: resolve does not pierce destiny
outline.gist: The third aphorism: strong resolve cannot break the walls of decree, yet you are still required to strive with energy.
