34:22.ar: قُلِ ٱدۡعُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمۡتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا لَهُمۡ فِيهِمَا مِن شِرۡكࣲ وَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡهُم مِّن ظَهِيرࣲ‏
34:22.en: Say (O Muhammad): Call upon those whom ye set up beside Allah! They possess not an atom's weight either in the heavens or in the earth, nor have they any share in either, nor hath He an auxiliary among them

34:23.ar: وَلَا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا لِمَنۡ أَذِنَ لَهُۥۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَن قُلُوبِهِمۡ قَالُواْ مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ
34:23.en: No intercession availeth with Him save for him whom He permitteth. Yet, when fear is banished from their hearts, they say: What was it that your Lord said? They say: The Truth. And He is the Sublime, the Great

34:24.ar: ۞قُلۡ مَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۖ وَإِنَّآ أَوۡ إِيَّاكُمۡ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
34:24.en: Say: Who giveth you provision from the sky and the earth? Say: Allah, Lo! we or you assuredly are rightly guided or in error manifest

34:25.ar: قُل لَّا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّآ أَجۡرَمۡنَا وَلَا نُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
34:25.en: Say: Ye will not be asked of what we committed, nor shall we be asked of what ye do

34:26.ar: قُلۡ يَجۡمَعُ بَيۡنَنَا رَبُّنَا ثُمَّ يَفۡتَحُ بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَهُوَ ٱلۡفَتَّاحُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
34:26.en: Say: Our Lord will bring us all together, then He will judge between us with truth. He is the All-knowing Judge

34:1.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَهُ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
34:1.en: Praise be to Allah, unto Whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. His is the praise in the Hereafter, and He is the Wise, the Aware

34:2.ar: يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعۡرُجُ فِيهَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلرَّحِيمُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
34:2.en: He knoweth that which goeth into the earth and that which cometh forth from it, and that descendeth from the heaven and that which ascendeth into it. He is the Merciful, the Forgiving

34:3.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَا تَأۡتِينَا ٱلسَّاعَةُۖ قُلۡ بَلَىٰ وَرَبِّي لَتَأۡتِيَنَّكُمۡ عَٰلِمِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ لَا يَعۡزُبُ عَنۡهُ مِثۡقَالُ ذَرَّةࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَآ أَصۡغَرُ مِن ذَٰلِكَ وَلَآ أَكۡبَرُ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
34:3.en: Those who disbelieve say: The Hour will never come unto us. Say: Nay, by my Lord, but it is coming unto you surely. (He is) the Knower of the Unseen. Not an atom's weight, or less than that or greater, escapeth Him in the heavens or in the earth, but it is in a clear Record

34:4.ar: لِّيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَرِزۡقࣱ كَرِيمࣱ‏
34:4.en: That He may reward those who believe and do good works. For them is pardon and a rich provision

34:5.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ سَعَوۡ فِيٓ ءَايَٰتِنَا مُعَٰجِزِينَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ مِّن رِّجۡزٍ أَلِيمࣱ‏
34:5.en: But those who strive against Our revelations, challenging (Us), theirs will be a painful doom of wrath

34:6.ar: وَيَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَيَهۡدِيٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَمِيدِ
34:6.en: Those who have been given knowledge see that what is revealed unto thee from thy Lord is the truth and leadeth unto the path of the Mighty, the Owner of Praise

34:7.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هَلۡ نَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ رَجُلࣲ يُنَبِّئُكُمۡ إِذَا مُزِّقۡتُمۡ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ إِنَّكُمۡ لَفِي خَلۡقࣲ جَدِيدٍ
34:7.en: Those who disbelieve say: Shall we show you a man who will tell you (that) when ye have become dispersed in dust with most complete dispersal still, even then, ye will be created anew

34:8.ar: أَفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا أَم بِهِۦ جِنَّةُۢۗ بَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ وَٱلضَّلَٰلِ ٱلۡبَعِيدِ
34:8.en: Hath he invented a lie concerning Allah, or is there in him a madness? Nay, but those who disbelieve in the Hereafter are in torment and far error

34:9.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِن نَّشَأۡ نَخۡسِفۡ بِهِمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ أَوۡ نُسۡقِطۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ كِسَفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّكُلِّ عَبۡدࣲ مُّنِيبࣲ‏
34:9.en: Have they not observed what is before them and what is behind them of the sky and the earth? If We will, We can make the earth swallow them, or cause obliteration from the sky to fall on them. Lo! herein surely is a portent for every slave who turneth (to Allah) repentant

34:10.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا دَاوُۥدَ مِنَّا فَضۡلࣰ اۖ يَٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُۥ وَٱلطَّيۡرَۖ وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلۡحَدِيدَ
34:10.en: And assuredly We gave David grace from Us, (saying): O ye hills and birds, echo his psalms of praise! And We made the iron supple unto him

34:11.ar: أَنِ ٱعۡمَلۡ سَٰبِغَٰتࣲ وَقَدِّرۡ فِي ٱلسَّرۡدِۖ وَٱعۡمَلُواْ صَٰلِحًاۖ إِنِّي بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
34:11.en: Saying: Make thou long coats of mail and measure the links (thereof). And do ye right. Lo! I am Seer of what ye do

34:12.ar: وَلِسُلَيۡمَٰنَ ٱلرِّيحَ غُدُوُّهَا شَهۡرࣱ وَرَوَاحُهَا شَهۡرࣱۖ وَأَسَلۡنَا لَهُۥ عَيۡنَ ٱلۡقِطۡرِۖ وَمِنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ مَن يَعۡمَلُ بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ بِإِذۡنِ رَبِّهِۦۖ وَمَن يَزِغۡ مِنۡهُمۡ عَنۡ أَمۡرِنَا نُذِقۡهُ مِنۡ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
34:12.en: And unto Solomon (We gave) the wind, whereof the morning course was a month's journey and the evening course a month's journey, and We caused the fount of copper to gush forth for him, and (We gave him) certain of the jinn who worked before him by permission of his Lord. And such of them as deviated from Our command, them We caused to taste the punishment of flaming Fire

34:13.ar: يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَٰرِيبَ وَتَمَٰثِيلَ وَجِفَانࣲ كَٱلۡجَوَابِ وَقُدُورࣲ رَّاسِيَٰتٍۚ ٱعۡمَلُوٓاْ ءَالَ دَاوُۥدَ شُكۡرࣰ اۚ وَقَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡ عِبَادِيَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
34:13.en: They made for him what he willed: synagogues and statues, basins like wells and boilers built into the ground. Give thanks, O House of David! Few of My bondmen are thankful

34:14.ar: فَلَمَّا قَضَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ مَا دَلَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَوۡتِهِۦٓ إِلَّا دَآبَّةُ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ تَأۡكُلُ مِنسَأَتَهُۥۖ فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ ٱلۡجِنُّ أَن لَّوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ مَا لَبِثُواْ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡمُهِينِ
34:14.en: And when We decreed death for him, nothing showed his death to them save a creeping creature of the earth which gnawed away his staff. And when he fell the jinn saw clearly how, if they had known the Unseen, they would not have continued in despised toil

34:15.ar: لَقَدۡ كَانَ لِسَبَإࣲ فِي مَسۡكَنِهِمۡ ءَايَةࣱۖ جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينࣲ وَشِمَالࣲۖ كُلُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِ رَبِّكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لَهُۥۚ بَلۡدَةࣱ طَيِّبَةࣱ وَرَبٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
34:15.en: There was indeed a sign for Sheba in their dwelling-place: Two gardens on the right hand and the left (as who should say): Eat of the provision of your Lord and render thanks to Him. A fair land and an indulgent Lord

34:16.ar: فَأَعۡرَضُواْ فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَيۡلَ ٱلۡعَرِمِ وَبَدَّلۡنَٰهُم بِجَنَّتَيۡهِمۡ جَنَّتَيۡنِ ذَوَاتَيۡ أُكُلٍ خَمۡطࣲ وَأَثۡلࣲ وَشَيۡءࣲ مِّن سِدۡرࣲ قَلِيلࣲ‏
34:16.en: But they were froward, so We sent on them the flood of 'Iram, and in exchange for their two gardens gave them two gardens bearing bitter fruit, the tamarisk and here and there a lote-tree

34:17.ar: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَيۡنَٰهُم بِمَا كَفَرُواْۖ وَهَلۡ نُجَٰزِيٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡكَفُورَ
34:17.en: This We awarded them because of their ingratitude. Punish We ever any save the ingrates

34:18.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلۡقُرَى ٱلَّتِي بَٰرَكۡنَا فِيهَا قُرࣰ ى ظَٰهِرَةࣰ وَقَدَّرۡنَا فِيهَا ٱلسَّيۡرَۖ سِيرُواْ فِيهَا لَيَالِيَ وَأَيَّامًا ءَامِنِينَ
34:18.en: And We set, between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns easy to be seen, and We made the stage between them easy, (saying): Travel in them safely both by night and day

34:19.ar: فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا بَٰعِدۡ بَيۡنَ أَسۡفَارِنَا وَظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ أَحَادِيثَ وَمَزَّقۡنَٰهُمۡ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارࣲ شَكُورࣲ‏
34:19.en: But they said: Our Lord! Make the stage between our journeys longer. And they wronged themselves, therefore We made them bywords (in the land) and scattered them abroad, a total scattering. Lo! herein verily are portents for each steadfast, grateful (heart)

34:20.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَّقَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ إِبۡلِيسُ ظَنَّهُۥ فَٱتَّبَعُوهُ إِلَّا فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
34:20.en: And Satan indeed found his calculation true concerning them, for they follow him, all save a group of true believers

34:21.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِم مِّن سُلۡطَٰنٍ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِمَّنۡ هُوَ مِنۡهَا فِي شَكࣲّۗ وَرَبُّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٍ حَفِيظࣱ‏
34:21.en: And he had no warrant whatsoever against them, save that We would know him who believeth in the Hereafter from him who is in doubt thereof; and thy Lord (O Muhammad) taketh note of all things

112:1.en: Say: He is Allah, the One

33:14.ar: وَلَوۡ دُخِلَتۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنۡ أَقۡطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةَ لَأٓتَوۡهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِهَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرࣰ ا
33:14.en: If the enemy had entered from all sides and they had been exhorted to treachery, they would have committed it, and would have hesitated thereupon but little

2:219.ar: ۞يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡخَمۡرِ وَٱلۡمَيۡسِرِۖ قُلۡ فِيهِمَآ إِثۡمࣱ كَبِيرࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَإِثۡمُهُمَآ أَكۡبَرُ مِن نَّفۡعِهِمَاۗ وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَۖ قُلِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ
2:219.en: They question thee about strong drink and games of chance. Say: In both is great sin, and (some) utility for men; but the sin of them is greater than their usefulness. And they ask thee what they ought to spend. Say: that which is superfluous. Thus Allah maketh plain to you (His) revelations, that haply ye may reflect

53:26.ar: ۞وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ لَا تُغۡنِي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَن يَأۡذَنَ ٱللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَرۡضَىٰٓ
53:26.en: And how many angels are in the heavens whose intercession availeth naught save after Allah giveth leave to whom He chooseth and accepteth

43:81.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَلَدࣱ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡعَٰبِدِينَ
43:81.en: Say (O Muhammad): If the Beneficent One hath a son, then, I shall be first among the worshippers. (But there is no son)

Z9dGfANIrms.speaker_note: continues his Sunday English tafseer of Surah Saba at the London Muslim Mosque, recaps his previous session and takes attendee questions
Z9dGfANIrms.title: Tafseer of Surah Saba, Session 5 (34:22-26)
Z9dGfANIrms.one_line: The 'Say' verses of Saba: how Muslim societies speak to others, nothing is truly ours, intercession only by permission, humility before al-Kabir, and agreeing to disagree.
Z9dGfANIrms.summary: He explains that clusters of verses beginning with 'Say' set Muslims' public attitude and terms of dialogue with other groups, and recaps the surah's theme: societies submit through gratitude given without a price tag, and need full certainty in the Hereafter, since any doubt surfaces under pressure, as with those in al-Ahzab who would have yielded after brief hesitation. The first 'Say' is ideological: whatever others call upon owns not an atom, shares nothing and helps Allah in nothing. National borders and resources are ours only figuratively, so a society must share what it can spare, though people may still fight to reclaim what was taken from them; he adds the limits of charity from Sa'd's will. Intercession happens only by Allah's permission, cannot cancel the rights of those you harmed, and is no free ticket, as the Prophet's words at the Pool show. Al-Ali and al-Kabir lead him to names we do not imitate: greatness and arrogance belong to Allah alone, an atom of arrogance bars paradise, and you are not the centre of the story. Arrogant societies have spilled oceans of blood. Finally, the verses model a non-bigoted stance: one of us is guided, outcomes will show which, you will not answer for our deeds, and Allah will judge between us.

outline.heading: Clusters of 'Say' verses
outline.gist: Verses beginning with 'Say' in a row set either a mode of dialogue, an outlook or a public attitude toward another group, depending on who is addressed, as in al-Ikhlas and al-Kafirun.

outline.heading: Recap: how societies submit
outline.gist: The surah's opening on praise, the Hereafter and knowledge, then the contrast of Dawud and Sulayman's kingdom with Saba, define societal submission as gratitude.

outline.heading: No national act of kindness without a price tag
outline.gist: Individuals give freely, but when one country builds another it always comes with a heavy hidden price; Muslim societies are meant to give back, not waste and not harm, for Allah's sake.

outline.heading: Recap: Iblis and the line between certainty and doubt
outline.gist: Iblis exists to separate those certain of the Hereafter from those with any doubt; there are only those two categories.

outline.heading: No camera or law can replace the Hereafter
outline.gist: When you have the lower hand, only belief that you will be resurrected and asked keeps you a good citizen; integrity is eroding even in wealthy countries.

outline.heading: Small doubt is exposed in hardship
outline.gist: In ease the person with five percent doubt and the one with ninety-five behave the same; when your life is on the line the doubt surfaces.

outline.heading: Holding out only a little while
outline.gist: In al-Ahzab, those who would have abandoned their faith after brief hesitation show that partial doubt only buys a few more seconds of standing.

outline.heading: A foot in both worlds will be tested
outline.gist: Hedging bets on the Hereafter does not work; Allah will put you to the test, and if you think you were never tested you may have failed without noticing.

outline.heading: The dialogue with other societies
outline.gist: Verses 22 to 30 set ideological, social, ethical and behavioural terms for how Muslim societies relate to those who believe and live differently.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verse 22.

outline.heading: Reading 'Say' through the theme of the surah
outline.gist: Context tells you who is addressed; here it is societies, the two models already given being Dawud and Sulayman's and Saba's.

outline.heading: Call on those you claim besides Allah
outline.gist: The ideological challenge: if anyone else owns any of the universe or answers prayer, call on them.

outline.heading: Dharrah: the smallest thing known
outline.gist: Once the ant's egg, the word has always meant the smallest thing people could perceive, so its referent shifted as science saw smaller things.

outline.heading: No ownership, no partnership, no helper
outline.gist: They own not an atom, have no share in anything, and Allah uses none of them to protect or help Him run the universe.

outline.heading: Our land and resources are ours only figuratively
outline.gist: Neither governments, borders nor ethnic claims give real ownership; small groups sitting on vast resources have no more right to them than anyone else.

outline.heading: So use it for everyone's benefit
outline.gist: Because you do not truly own it, gratitude means using what Allah gave you for the betterment of others, or He takes away the barakah.

outline.heading: Show gratitude before you argue
outline.gist: If other societies are more philanthropic than we are, we should stay quiet until we do our due diligence; the argument only stands when we live it.

outline.heading: Question: what about those dispossessed of their land?
outline.gist: Gratitude does not mean giving away the water you need; it means sharing what you can spare instead of hoarding or monopolising, and the oppressed may fight for their rights.

outline.heading: Give from what is surplus
outline.gist: Charity comes from what exceeds your needs; the Prophet told Sa'd to leave his heirs well off, and a deathbed attempt to give everything away is legally blocked.

outline.heading: How easily barakah is removed
outline.gist: Allah need not take the land or water; He simply leaves trees that bear no edible fruit, as with Saba.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verse 23 and settles the English word as intercession.

outline.heading: Intercession only by His permission
outline.gist: Intercession on the Day of Judgment never overrides Allah's will; it shows the rank of the righteous, and the Prophet will intercede until the gates close.

outline.heading: No free ticket, and no cancelling others' rights
outline.gist: Gambling on intercession while living as you please has no evidence; it covers sins left unrepented, not harm done to people, which must be settled with them.

outline.heading: You do not know what they did after you
outline.gist: At the Pool the Prophet will be told that some companions changed after him and will not intercede for those Allah is displeased with.

outline.heading: The pious interceding for their families
outline.gist: The righteous, including those who carry the Quran, will intercede for family; the narrations are somewhat weak but widely used and motivating.

outline.heading: When the fear is lifted from their hearts
outline.gist: On that Day everyone is consumed by fear for himself; only when the righteous sense relief do they ask what their Lord has said and look for relatives they might help.

outline.heading: Al-Ali: the one no ruling can override
outline.gist: Since intercession involves rank, Allah names Himself the Most High: no one lower can overrule His decision.

outline.heading: Al-Kabir and al-Mutakabbir
outline.gist: Al-Kabir shares a root with kibr; seeing oneself above all is right only for Allah and goes against human nature as a servant.

outline.heading: Names we do not imitate
outline.gist: We emulate His mercy, generosity and patience, but names like al-Kabir, al-Mutakabbir and al-Qawiyy are only for knowing Him; humility would be against His nature.

outline.heading: Accept that you are a servant
outline.gist: Your nafs resists hearing it, but the sooner you accept being a servant of the Great, the happier and better a Muslim you will be; wanting to be above others needs fixing.

outline.heading: An atom of arrogance bars paradise
outline.gist: The hadith that no one with an atom's weight of arrogance enters paradise, because nothing against your nature can enter it.

outline.heading: You are not the centre of the story
outline.gist: Not even of your spouse's life or your own; it is Allah's story, so play your role in it and stop making it about yourself.

outline.heading: What happens when societies become arrogant
outline.gist: Four centuries of history show bloodshed, oppression and neglect of millions whenever a group decides it is better than others.

outline.heading: Does having more make me better?
outline.gist: Competition is good, but faster cars, bigger houses and better universities do not make you better; taqwa cannot be measured and Allah reveals rank only when you no longer care.

outline.heading: Compete to please Him
outline.gist: Compete in pleasing Allah without being preoccupied with whether you are better; societies need this humility.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verse 24, the practical second 'Say'.

outline.heading: Who provides from the sky and the earth?
outline.gist: All provision and wealth around you comes from Allah alone.

outline.heading: Either we or you are rightly guided
outline.gist: A Muslim is never a bigot closed to change; evidence, reason and the outcomes of behaviour, not mere opinion, will show who is guided.

outline.heading: Societies are judged by outcomes
outline.gist: Personally, Allah's word is enough, but between communities behaviours must be judged by whether they helped; this is the attitude of dialogue.

outline.heading: If the Most Merciful had a son
outline.gist: A parallel at the end of az-Zukhruf: prove it and I will be the first to worship him; otherwise keep to the basic understanding of a supreme being.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verses 25 and 26.

outline.heading: You will not be asked about our crimes
outline.gist: The verse concedes their premise for argument's sake while calling their own conduct only 'what you do': each answers for himself.

outline.heading: Tolerance: agreeing to disagree
outline.gist: Accepting that Muslims see things differently from other groups is part of being Muslim; there is nothing wrong with difference.

outline.heading: Our Lord will gather us and judge
outline.gist: Al-Fattah, the All-Knowing, will separate truth from falsehood where they are now mixed together.

34:15.ar: لَقَدۡ كَانَ لِسَبَإࣲ فِي مَسۡكَنِهِمۡ ءَايَةࣱۖ جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينࣲ وَشِمَالࣲۖ كُلُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِ رَبِّكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لَهُۥۚ بَلۡدَةࣱ طَيِّبَةࣱ وَرَبٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
34:15.en: There was indeed a sign for Sheba in their dwelling-place: Two gardens on the right hand and the left (as who should say): Eat of the provision of your Lord and render thanks to Him. A fair land and an indulgent Lord

34:16.ar: فَأَعۡرَضُواْ فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَيۡلَ ٱلۡعَرِمِ وَبَدَّلۡنَٰهُم بِجَنَّتَيۡهِمۡ جَنَّتَيۡنِ ذَوَاتَيۡ أُكُلٍ خَمۡطࣲ وَأَثۡلࣲ وَشَيۡءࣲ مِّن سِدۡرࣲ قَلِيلࣲ‏
34:16.en: But they were froward, so We sent on them the flood of 'Iram, and in exchange for their two gardens gave them two gardens bearing bitter fruit, the tamarisk and here and there a lote-tree

34:17.ar: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَيۡنَٰهُم بِمَا كَفَرُواْۖ وَهَلۡ نُجَٰزِيٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡكَفُورَ
34:17.en: This We awarded them because of their ingratitude. Punish We ever any save the ingrates

34:18.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلۡقُرَى ٱلَّتِي بَٰرَكۡنَا فِيهَا قُرࣰ ى ظَٰهِرَةࣰ وَقَدَّرۡنَا فِيهَا ٱلسَّيۡرَۖ سِيرُواْ فِيهَا لَيَالِيَ وَأَيَّامًا ءَامِنِينَ
34:18.en: And We set, between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns easy to be seen, and We made the stage between them easy, (saying): Travel in them safely both by night and day

34:19.ar: فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا بَٰعِدۡ بَيۡنَ أَسۡفَارِنَا وَظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ أَحَادِيثَ وَمَزَّقۡنَٰهُمۡ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارࣲ شَكُورࣲ‏
34:19.en: But they said: Our Lord! Make the stage between our journeys longer. And they wronged themselves, therefore We made them bywords (in the land) and scattered them abroad, a total scattering. Lo! herein verily are portents for each steadfast, grateful (heart)

34:20.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَّقَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ إِبۡلِيسُ ظَنَّهُۥ فَٱتَّبَعُوهُ إِلَّا فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
34:20.en: And Satan indeed found his calculation true concerning them, for they follow him, all save a group of true believers

34:21.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِم مِّن سُلۡطَٰنٍ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِمَّنۡ هُوَ مِنۡهَا فِي شَكࣲّۗ وَرَبُّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٍ حَفِيظࣱ‏
34:21.en: And he had no warrant whatsoever against them, save that We would know him who believeth in the Hereafter from him who is in doubt thereof; and thy Lord (O Muhammad) taketh note of all things

34:13.ar: يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَٰرِيبَ وَتَمَٰثِيلَ وَجِفَانࣲ كَٱلۡجَوَابِ وَقُدُورࣲ رَّاسِيَٰتٍۚ ٱعۡمَلُوٓاْ ءَالَ دَاوُۥدَ شُكۡرࣰ اۚ وَقَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡ عِبَادِيَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
34:13.en: They made for him what he willed: synagogues and statues, basins like wells and boilers built into the ground. Give thanks, O House of David! Few of My bondmen are thankful

68:17.ar: إِنَّا بَلَوۡنَٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّهَا مُصۡبِحِينَ
68:17.en: Lo! We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning

68:18.en: And made no exception (for the Will of Allah)

68:19.ar: فَطَافَ عَلَيۡهَا طَآئِفࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمۡ نَآئِمُونَ
68:19.en: Then a visitation from thy Lord came upon it while they slept

68:20.en: And in the morning it was as if plucked

68:21.en: And they cried out one unto another in the morning

68:22.ar: أَنِ ٱغۡدُواْ عَلَىٰ حَرۡثِكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰرِمِينَ
68:22.en: Saying: Run unto your field if ye would pluck (the fruit)

68:23.en: So they went off, saying one unto another in low tones

68:24.ar: أَن لَّا يَدۡخُلَنَّهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّسۡكِينࣱ‏
68:24.en: No needy man shall enter it to-day against you

68:25.en: They went betimes, strong in (this) purpose

68:26.en: But when they saw it, they said: Lo! we are in error

106:2.en: For their taming (We cause) the caravans to set forth in winter and summer

17:62.ar: قَالَ أَرَءَيۡتَكَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كَرَّمۡتَ عَلَيَّ لَئِنۡ أَخَّرۡتَنِ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَأَحۡتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
17:62.en: He said: Seest Thou this (creature) whom Thou hast honoured above me, if Thou give me grace until the Day of Resurrection I verily will seize his seed, save but a few

7:16.ar: قَالَ فَبِمَآ أَغۡوَيۡتَنِي لَأَقۡعُدَنَّ لَهُمۡ صِرَٰطَكَ ٱلۡمُسۡتَقِيمَ
7:16.en: He said: Now, because Thou hast sent me astray, verily I shall lurk in ambush for them on Thy Right Path

7:17.ar: ثُمَّ لَأٓتِيَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ وَعَنۡ أَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡ وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمۡۖ وَلَا تَجِدُ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ شَٰكِرِينَ
7:17.en: Then I shall come upon them from before them and from behind them and from their right hands and from their left hands, and Thou wilt not find most of them beholden (unto Thee)

-CmenB1L_Gc.title: Tafseer of Surah Saba, Session 4 (34:15-21)
-CmenB1L_Gc.one_line: The fall of Saba: gratitude as a society's submission, spite after losing blessings, Iblis's assumption proved true, and certainty in the Hereafter.
-CmenB1L_Gc.summary: Saba treats submission at the level of societies, and he contrasts Dawud and Sulayman's grateful kingdom with the people of Saba. A society submits by using what it has for good and by gratitude: not wasting, not harming, giving back. Saba refused, so the flood replaced their orchards with bitter, fruitless trees; kufr here means refusing to recognise a blessing. He warns of societies, and individuals, who keep the rules only while things go their way, and widens this to international debt and the erosion of social safety nets. Even after the punishment Allah left Saba a safe trade route north through visible towns, yet ingratitude is a mentality that loss does not cure; they asked Allah to lengthen their journeys out of spite, like a child smashing his own toys or a gamer throwing the game, and were scattered into mere stories. People live either in patience or in gratitude, with no neutral state. Iblis assumed most humans would be ungrateful, and every lapse proves him right, though he has no control over anyone. He exists so that true certainty in the Hereafter can be distinguished from doubt, because belief in accountability only shows under hardship and no society holds its morals without it. He closes with an aphorism from Ibn Ata'illah.

outline.heading: Opening
Saba: submission at the level of societies
outline.gist: Individuals submit in many different ways, but societies submit in the same few ways; the surah compares the kingdom of Dawud and Sulayman with the people of Saba.

outline.heading: How a society submits: good use and gratitude
outline.gist: The two words from the first story: use what you have for good, and show gratitude by not wasting, not harming and giving back.

outline.heading: Saba's prosperity and the flood
outline.gist: A rich, secure, advanced civilisation in Yemen was told to eat and be grateful; they turned away, and the flood left their two orchards growing only bitter and fruitless trees: the barakah was gone.

outline.heading: Kufr as refusing to recognise a blessing
outline.gist: At its root kufr is refusing to acknowledge a blessing; carried all the way to denying that life itself is from Allah it becomes disbelief.

outline.heading: Nothing in this world is a punishment unless you make it one
outline.gist: Any hardship can become a blessing if you respond well; even a deserved slap is only a punishment if you refuse to wake up.

outline.heading: Keeping the rules only when things go well
outline.gist: A society or person who stops being kind and law-abiding once things go badly was doing good for the wrong reason all along.

outline.heading: The orchard owners who repented
outline.gist: Unlike Saba, the brothers who lost their father's orchard admitted their mistake and repented; Saba took a different, frightening path.

outline.heading: Easy to be good when you are comfortable
outline.gist: Being good while wealthy, healthy and unstressed is not submission; the test is how you behave when you do not get your way.

outline.heading: Giving without waiting for a return
outline.gist: A submissive society stands by others for Allah's sake, not for gain; that is the difference from societies that help only when something comes back.

outline.heading: The dirtiest politics are international
outline.gist: Indebted nations living in luxury, others starving, and health care and social security eroded by debt; those of us in a country with public health care and education rarely see it.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verses 18 and 19 and explains a stopping rule for the reciter.

outline.heading: Forced to trade: origin of the caravan journeys
outline.gist: No longer self-sufficient, Saba had to trade with the richer north, the beginning of the caravan routes the Quraysh later travelled.

outline.heading: The blessed towns of Sham
outline.gist: The towns Allah blessed are those of the grateful kingdom of Dawud and Sulayman in Jerusalem and around it.

outline.heading: Visible towns along the route
outline.gist: Stops between Yemen and Sham made a thousand-kilometre journey possible, the same line through Makkah and Madinah used for generations.

outline.heading: How hard the basics were to come by
outline.gist: A pair of shoes made you wealthy, grain and armour were scarce and raids were constant, so safe stops to trade were a great blessing.

outline.heading: Allah did not take everything away
outline.gist: Told to travel safely by night and day, Saba had to work harder for less, but they could still make a living.

outline.heading: Ingratitude is a mentality
outline.gist: Having more or less does not change an ungrateful person; taking a child's toys away will not make him grateful, and Allah instead made Saba work harder.

outline.heading: Lord, lengthen our journeys
outline.gist: Rather than acknowledging their past ingratitude, they asked Allah to make their journeys longer.

outline.heading: Spite: smashing your own toys
outline.gist: Like a child breaking his remaining toys or a gamer throwing the game, people who do not get their way turn hateful and petty, a pattern he sees most in older people.

outline.heading: They knew their Lord and still wronged themselves
outline.gist: They addressed Allah directly, so their kufr was ingratitude, not disbelief; in defying Him they only wronged themselves.

outline.heading: Made into tales and torn apart
outline.gist: Saba became nothing but stories and were scattered in every direction, echoing the surah's opening on the dead torn apart and brought back, as nations can be restored.

outline.heading: Patience or gratitude: no third state
outline.gist: Signs for every patient and grateful person: you are either persevering through difficulty or grateful in ease; feeling neutral means you should be grateful.

outline.heading: Refusing patience or gratitude only harms you
outline.gist: Spite punishes no one but yourself; Saba became more bitter and lost everything until generations later.

outline.heading: Bilqis before or after?
outline.gist: Historians differ whether Bilqis and Sulayman came before or after this catastrophe; either way the lesson matters more, and the Arabs of the peninsula spread from Saba.

outline.heading: How societies react when barakah is lost
outline.gist: Societies that should be grateful and societies that should be patient are both failing today.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verses 20 and 21, among his favourite verses in the Quran.

outline.heading: Iblis's assumption
outline.gist: Iblis vowed to mislead Adam's children and said Allah would not find most of them grateful; it was his guess, not certainty.

outline.heading: Allah's answer to the challenge
outline.gist: Iblis claimed Allah's judgment of Adam was wrong; Allah knew that among humans would be some so selfless, grateful and patient that they make up for the rest.

outline.heading: Do not prove your enemy right
outline.gist: Every act of ingratitude walks the path Iblis drew and proves him right; no one likes to prove an enemy right.

outline.heading: Proving someone wrong as motivation
outline.gist: Telling a stubborn child he will fail can drive him to succeed; he was played this way as a child, and a cousin starved abroad for years rather than prove his father right.

outline.heading: Whose expectations will you meet?
outline.gist: Iblis set expectations for you and so did Allah; you are able to meet either, and you choose which one you prove right.

outline.heading: Except a group of believers
outline.gist: There will always be believers who refuse to walk Iblis's road and fulfil their covenant.

outline.heading: Iblis has no control
outline.gist: Sultan at its root is control, and Iblis had none over those who followed him.

outline.heading: Why Iblis exists at all
outline.gist: An alternative must be on offer for an infinite reward to be fair; angels with only one choice are not given paradise.

outline.heading: Suggestions, not force
outline.gist: Iblis is no force of nature; he only makes suggestions and raises expectations, and the exception that follows explains his purpose.

outline.heading: So that We may know: knowledge you will accept
outline.gist: Allah already knows, but you would never accept being judged for deeds you did not commit; life makes His knowledge something the other party accepts.

outline.heading: Gratitude, the Hereafter and knowledge
outline.gist: Echoing the surah's opening, a society needs gratitude, belief in the Hereafter and knowledge; no number of cameras makes people behave without that inner motivation.

outline.heading: Certainty or doubt, nothing in between
outline.gist: The line is drawn between certainty and doubt, not belief and disbelief; any doubt sits with everything else. Al-Hafiz encompasses all.

outline.heading: Belief in the Hereafter shows only in hardship
outline.gist: When you are prosperous, following the rules may be self-serving: the rich want theft forbidden because they have the most to lose.

outline.heading: Doubt surfaces at the moment of temptation
outline.gist: Facing fifty thousand you should not take while in debt, or a truth that could cost you, only certainty in accountability stops you.

outline.heading: Ten percent doubt equals ninety
outline.gist: Before Allah any amount of doubt is the same; you will be put in enough situations to prove to yourself whether you are certain.

outline.heading: No society keeps its morals without the Hereafter
outline.gist: If you only live once and are poor among the corrupt rich, morality has no answer; he has yet to see a faithless society keep its ethics through hardship.

outline.heading: Ibn Ata'illah: striving for what is guaranteed
outline.gist: Effort spent on what Allah has already taken care of, while neglecting what He asked of you, shows the inner sight has dimmed; he will explain basirah next time.

59:1.ar: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
59:1.en: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifieth Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

59:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ لِأَوَّلِ ٱلۡحَشۡرِۚ مَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْۖ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمۡ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ فَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَمۡ يَحۡتَسِبُواْۖ وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعۡبَۚ يُخۡرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَأَيۡدِي ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ فَٱعۡتَبِرُواْ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
59:2.en: He it is Who hath caused those of the People of the Scripture who disbelieved to go forth from their homes unto the first exile. Ye deemed not that they would go forth, while they deemed that their strongholds would protect them from Allah. But Allah reached them from a place whereof they recked not, and cast terror in their hearts so that they ruined their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So learn a lesson, O ye who have eyes

59:3.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡجَلَآءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابُ ٱلنَّارِ
59:3.en: And if Allah had not decreed migration for them, He verily would have punished them in the world, and theirs in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire

59:4.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ شَآقُّواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۖ وَمَن يُشَآقِّ ٱللَّهَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:4.en: That is because they were opposed to Allah and His messenger; and whoso is opposed to Allah, (for him) verily Allah is stern in reprisal

59:5.ar: مَا قَطَعۡتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوۡ تَرَكۡتُمُوهَا قَآئِمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيُخۡزِيَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
59:5.en: Whatsoever palm-trees ye cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah's leave, in order that He might confound the evil-livers

59:6.ar: وَمَآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡهُمۡ فَمَآ أَوۡجَفۡتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ خَيۡلࣲ وَلَا رِكَابࣲ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسَلِّطُ رُسُلَهُۥ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
59:6.en: And that which Allah gave as spoil unto His messenger from them, ye urged not any horse or riding-camel for the sake thereof, but Allah giveth His messenger lordship over whom He will. Allah is Able to do all things

59:7.ar: مَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ فَلِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ كَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةَۢ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأَغۡنِيَآءِ مِنكُمۡۚ وَمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَىٰكُمۡ عَنۡهُ فَٱنتَهُواْۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:7.en: That which Allah giveth as spoil unto His messenger from the people of the townships, it is for Allah and His messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, that it become not a commodity between the rich among you. And whatsoever the messenger giveth you, take it. And whatsoever he forbiddeth, abstain (from it). And keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is stern in reprisal

XFmrKHDuOmA.title: Seerah Halaqah, October 13, 2018 (Part 1): The Expulsion of Banu al-Nadir
XFmrKHDuOmA.one_line: After Uhud the tribes grow bold; Banu al-Nadir plot to kill the Prophet, are besieged and expelled, read through Surat al-Hashr.
XFmrKHDuOmA.summary: He opens by tracing how the archers' mistake at Uhud kept costing the Muslims: the losses of the battle and the betrayals that followed, as tribes around Medina concluded the Muslims were weak. From this he draws a rule he wants people to keep: a choice affects you and others, directly and indirectly, for years, and you answer for it. He then tells the story of Banu al-Nadir, a Jewish tribe bound by the Medina charter, who corresponded with the Prophet's enemies and tried to drop a rock on him while he visited them. The Prophet verified rather than acted on reports, then ordered them to leave. Trusting their fortresses and promised allies, they held out, but panic and rumours broke them within weeks; they left, wrecking their own homes. He reads Surat al-Hashr to show that their forts could not protect them from Allah, that victory and defeat both come through doors no one expects, and that the right thing must be done even when it does not look like it will work. He closes with the Muslims' guilt over cutting a few small palms for firewood in a freezing winter siege, as proof of how seriously they took the ban on needless harm, and with how the spoils were distributed.

outline.heading: The lasting cost of the archers' mistake at Uhud
outline.gist: The losses at Uhud and the betrayals that followed all trace back to one disobedience, which made the surrounding tribes think the Muslims were weak.

outline.heading: Ripple effects: your choices are your most sacred trust
outline.gist: A decision affects you and others, short and long term, and you are held accountable for its consequences.

outline.heading: Banu al-Nadir and the Prophet's habit of visiting every tribe
outline.gist: Who the tribe was, where they lived, and how the Prophet kept relationships with every group in Medina.

outline.heading: Correspondence with the enemy and a plot to kill him
outline.gist: Intercepted messages showed the tribe discussing killing the Prophet quietly and making it look like an accident.

outline.heading: Why he verified before acting
outline.gist: With fewer than two thousand Muslims he avoided escalation and never acted on information alone, so he went to see for himself.

outline.heading: The rock on the rooftop
outline.gist: Two men tried to push a rock onto him from a roof; he left at once and returned to Medina.

outline.heading: Treason and the order to leave
outline.gist: He declared the charter broken and ordered them out, allowing them to take their property.

outline.heading: Holding out in their fortresses
outline.gist: A leader convinced them to stay behind their walled forts, expecting allies to come to their aid, which never happened.

outline.heading: The siege and the opening of Surat al-Hashr
outline.gist: The siege lasted around twenty days; he recites the opening verses praising Allah and describing their expulsion.

outline.heading: Al-Hashr: the time of choosing sides
outline.gist: Beyond the Day of Judgment, al-hashr means the gathering when Arabia began to choose sides, and everyone would soon have to pick one.

outline.heading: They thought their forts would protect them from Allah
outline.gist: Wealth, education and walls made their expulsion seem impossible, yet Allah came at them from where they did not expect.

outline.heading: Success and failure come through doors you never expected
outline.gist: Plan carefully, but most plans do not unfold as imagined; life turns in ways no one foresees.

outline.heading: Panic defeated them, not numbers
outline.gist: Rumours spread among them that their food would run out; fear did what the Muslims could not do by force.

outline.heading: The departure: destroying their own homes
outline.gist: They agreed to leave, and tore down their houses so the Muslims could not use them; the Prophet wanted no bloodshed.

outline.heading: Why they were punished
outline.gist: They opposed Allah and His Messenger, and the punishment of exile was harsh enough.

outline.heading: Do the right thing even when you cannot see it working
outline.gist: Victory comes in ways you would not imagine, so do not base your action on whether it looks possible.

outline.heading: A freezing winter siege
outline.gist: Desert winter nights were bitterly cold and the besiegers had no fuel while they stood guard.

outline.heading: Cutting the small palms and the guilt that followed
outline.gist: Taught never to harm a living thing or cut trees, they cut a few small palms for warmth and wondered whether that was why victory was delayed; the verse reassured them.

outline.heading: The mentality of the early Muslims
outline.gist: People who felt guilty over a tree were not looking to harm anyone; that was the character they carried.

outline.heading: Outnumbered, and where the tribe went
outline.gist: About 700 Muslims besieged around 2,000 armed people; after their exit some settled in Khaybar and others went north to Syria.

outline.heading: Distributing the spoils
outline.gist: He begins on how the abandoned property was divided so wealth would not circulate only among the rich.

33:45.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ شَٰهِدࣰ ا وَمُبَشِّرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ ا
33:45.en: O Prophet! Lo! We have sent thee as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner

33:46.ar: وَدَاعِيًا إِلَى ٱللَّهِ بِإِذۡنِهِۦ وَسِرَاجࣰ ا مُّنِيرࣰ ا
33:46.en: And as a summoner unto Allah by His permission, and as a lamp that giveth light

33:47.ar: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ فَضۡلࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
33:47.en: And announce unto the believers the good tidings that they will have great bounty from Allah

33:48.ar: وَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ وَدَعۡ أَذَىٰهُمۡ وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلࣰ ا
33:48.en: And incline not to the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Disregard their noxious talk, and put thy trust in Allah. Allah is sufficient as Trustee

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

2:143.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَسَطࣰ ا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ اۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:143.en: Thus We have appointed you a middle nation, that ye may be witnesses against mankind, and that the messenger may be a witness against you. And We appointed the qiblah which ye formerly observed only that We might know him who followeth the messenger, from him who turneth on his heels. In truth it was a hard (test) save for those whom Allah guided. But it was not Allah's purpose that your faith should be in vain, for Allah is Full of Pity, Merciful toward mankind

33:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
33:1.en: O Prophet! Keep thy duty to Allah and obey not the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise

SGcn8CQnRJk.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 15: Witness, Bearer of Good News and a Radiant Lamp (33:45-48)
SGcn8CQnRJk.one_line: The five descriptions of the Prophet in 33:45-46, with role modelling as the heart of dawah, and Ibn Ata'illah's second aphorism on balance.
SGcn8CQnRJk.summary: After recapping the surah's theme of obedience when it is hard, he explains why verses on the Prophet's status are placed between the stories of his private life. In 33:45-46 Allah gives him five descriptions. Shahid first means an example: his life proves that Allah's way works under worse conditions than ours, and believers must show the same proof or have no argument; the martyr is so named as the ultimate example of giving everything. He adds that a good intention never excuses a wrong action. As bearer of good news he began with hope before warning, and Paradise and Hell are set so far apart that the choice should be obvious. As caller to Allah, he taught mostly by conduct: he spoke little, and people were won by what they saw, so dawah today needs role models more than talks. As a radiant lamp, his presence itself drew people, as with Abdullah ibn Salam, and the greatest loss for Muslims is not having been with him. 33:47-48 give the believers good news and tell the Prophet not to obey the disbelievers, to leave their harm where it falls and rely on Allah. He closes with Ibn Ata'illah's aphorism on keeping to the station Allah has placed you in, between working through means and devotion.

outline.heading: The surah's theme: obeying when it is hard
outline.gist: Al-Ahzab opens a cluster of surahs on submission and approaches it through the hardest kind of obedience.

outline.heading: Recap: the Trench, the wives, women in the deen
outline.gist: Courage under extreme fear, the wives accepting a life without wealth, and the uncomfortable topics of women's conduct.

outline.heading: Recap: 33:36 and the marriage to Zaynab
outline.gist: No believer has a choice once Allah commands; the Prophet obeyed despite foreseeing the backlash, a different kind of trial from the slander of Aisha.

outline.heading: Recap: dhikr as the cure for distress
outline.gist: Dhikr is placed among the hard stories because remembering Allah in every decision removes distress at His commands.

outline.heading: Two kinds of remembrance
outline.gist: Private tasbih and remembering Allah throughout life; He should not be boxed inside the masjid.

outline.heading: Recap: blessings, light and a greeting of peace
outline.gist: Allah and His angels bless those who remember Him, bring them to light, and greet them with peace.

outline.heading: Why his status follows the private stories
outline.gist: Whenever the Quran mentions a lapse in his judgement, it affirms his status so no one doubts him; two more stories about his home are still to come.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:45-48 and counting the madd
outline.gist: He recites the passage and teaches holding each elongation mark for four counts.

outline.heading: "O Prophet": addressed with respect
outline.gist: Other prophets are called by name, but Muhammad is always addressed by title with ya ayyuha, a form that signals respect.

outline.heading: "Kafir" is a description, not an insult
outline.gist: The Quran's ya ayyuha even for disbelievers acknowledges them as a group; the word describes a belief position, as a non-Muslim would describe him.

outline.heading: Five descriptions, and beauty amid rulings
outline.gist: Madinan surahs heavy with rulings carry passages of pure beauty so hearts do not harden, as at the end of Al-Baqarah and Al-Ma'idah.

outline.heading: Shahid: how can he witness us?
outline.gist: Shahid is usually rendered martyr or witness, but he did not see our deeds; the word has a root meaning that explains both.

outline.heading: His life proves it works
outline.gist: When people say they cannot avoid zina, alcohol or interest, his life under harder conditions shows Allah's way can be lived.

outline.heading: We are witnesses too
outline.gist: Allah judges people by whether they had a living example; if we do not show that Islam works, others have no evidence of it.

outline.heading: Shahid means example
outline.gist: In Arabic grammar books a shahid is an illustrative example from poetry or the Quran; witness is derived from that root meaning.

outline.heading: "Show me how you are better"
outline.gist: Like a door-to-door missionary, an argument without visible results fails; if Muslims are not thriving ethically, the claim is crippled.

outline.heading: Why the martyr is called shahid
outline.gist: Life is irreplaceable, so whoever gives it for Allah is the ultimate example; living for Allah is still better.

outline.heading: Good intentions do not excuse wrong actions
outline.gist: An act needs both a sincere intention and a valid action, like the loving relative whose home remedy kills, or praying five rakat for maghrib out of love.

outline.heading: Do not wish to die in battle
outline.gist: Living for Allah is worth more; the Prophet told people not to wish to meet the enemy, and one who seeks death is looking at it wrongly.

outline.heading: He is the standard we are held to
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment we will be asked what was harder for us than for him; his most private life was exposed so we would have the example.

outline.heading: Bearer of good news first
outline.gist: His mission began with good tidings: the greatest good news is that your Lord is the Merciful, Forgiving and Loving.

outline.heading: Warner: the first public call
outline.gist: His public dawah began with say la ilaha illallah and you will succeed, before the harder warnings.

outline.heading: Why Paradise and Hell are opposites
outline.gist: If the alternative to Paradise were mere non-existence, few would strive; we plan trips to avoid any discomfort yet act as if we are fine with Hell.

outline.heading: It all comes down to belief in the Hereafter
outline.gist: Either you believe in resurrection, records and consequences or you do not; the rest follows from that.

outline.heading: Caller to Allah
outline.gist: Calling to Allah is the job of every prophet; the phrase is left open: to His way, His message, His love.

outline.heading: Dawah is role modelling
outline.gist: Talk is a small part of dawah; children absorb little of a lecture, as his son remembered only a man and a horse, but they copy what they see.

outline.heading: What children see, they repeat
outline.gist: Someone raised in an abusive home is far more likely to be abusive even when convinced violence is wrong; behaviour, not words, transfers.

outline.heading: He spoke little, and people loved him
outline.gist: He was often silent and spoke concisely; whoever saw him was awed and whoever lived with him loved him, because people sense genuineness.

outline.heading: What they saw him do
outline.gist: Carrying earth at the Trench, giving away his share of spoils, praying alone at night, standing closest to the enemy; words can be bent but actions cannot.

outline.heading: Be the role model yourself
outline.gist: Pick up the scattered shoes yourself, do what you think is missing, and hold back criticism; the community is saturated with talk.

outline.heading: A radiant lamp: what siraj means
outline.gist: Siraj is a lamp that radiates, related to the saddle that moves with a living horse: a presence felt though not touched.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Salam: not the face of a liar
outline.gist: A Jewish scholar and his son prepared all night to debate him, but on seeing his face the father said this is not the face of a liar and threw the plan away.

outline.heading: The greatest loss: not being with him
outline.gist: In every calamity one remembers it could be worse, and that the greatest calamity was losing the Prophet; if we do not feel this, we have not understood much.

outline.heading: Those who would give everything to see him
outline.gist: He said people at the end of time would believe in him without seeing him and wish to give family and wealth to see him.

outline.heading: The companion who walked away backwards
outline.gist: A man who met him only briefly walked backwards to keep looking at his face, fearing he might not see him again.

outline.heading: The companions undone by his death
outline.gist: Even Abu Bakr and Umar fell apart at his death, showing what his presence alone meant.

outline.heading: What the lamp adds to the other four
outline.gist: Nothing in the Quran is redundant: beyond his roles there was something in his presence and heart unlike anyone else.

outline.heading: People who carry his light
outline.gist: Those who live like him take on some of that radiance; we have all met a teacher or elder we wanted to stay near.

outline.heading: With those you love: Anas and Bilal
outline.gist: Anas rejoiced that a person will be with those he loves; Bilal smiled while dying because tomorrow he would meet the beloved and his companions.

outline.heading: The Ansari woman at Uhud
outline.gist: Told her husband, son and brother had died, she kept asking about the Prophet and said every calamity is small as long as he is safe.

outline.heading: Fadalah came to kill him in tawaf
outline.gist: He put his hand on Fadalah's chest, and the man who hated him most walked away loving him more than anyone.

outline.heading: Good news of a great bounty for believers
outline.gist: The glad tidings of a great reward from Allah are offered to all who believe.

outline.heading: Do not obey the disbelievers and hypocrites
outline.gist: Echoing the surah's opening, not obeying also means not imitating them or being drawn into their narrative after the slander over Zaynab.

outline.heading: Leave their harm where it falls
outline.gist: Treat people's insults like rubbish on the ground: do not carry them home or let them change you; criticism will always come.

outline.heading: Rely on Allah alone
outline.gist: After obeying and enduring the backlash, depend on Allah, who is sufficient as a guardian.

outline.heading: Ibn Ata'illah's second aphorism
outline.gist: Wanting pure devotion when Allah has placed you among means is a hidden desire; wanting means when He has placed you in devotion is a fall from a higher rank.

outline.heading: The world of means and the world of devotion
outline.gist: Muslims balance a world governed by causes, where work brings provision, and acts of worship that make no sense by worldly productivity.

outline.heading: Escaping duties into worship
outline.gist: A husband and father who sits in the masjid all day while his home, marriage and career collapse is not pious but running away, from fear of failure or love of praise.

outline.heading: The reverse error
outline.gist: When Allah asks for spiritual worship, such as wudu that seems pointless by worldly logic, insisting on worldly reasoning is also a fall.

34:24.ar: ۞قُلۡ مَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۖ وَإِنَّآ أَوۡ إِيَّاكُمۡ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
34:24.en: Say: Who giveth you provision from the sky and the earth? Say: Allah, Lo! we or you assuredly are rightly guided or in error manifest

34:25.ar: قُل لَّا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّآ أَجۡرَمۡنَا وَلَا نُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
34:25.en: Say: Ye will not be asked of what we committed, nor shall we be asked of what ye do

34:26.ar: قُلۡ يَجۡمَعُ بَيۡنَنَا رَبُّنَا ثُمَّ يَفۡتَحُ بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَهُوَ ٱلۡفَتَّاحُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
34:26.en: Say: Our Lord will bring us all together, then He will judge between us with truth. He is the All-knowing Judge

34:31.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَلَا بِٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِۗ وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ مَوۡقُوفُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ يَرۡجِعُ بَعۡضُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ يَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لَوۡلَآ أَنتُمۡ لَكُنَّا مُؤۡمِنِينَ
34:31.en: And those who disbelieve say: We believe not in this Qur'an nor in that which was before it; but oh, if thou couldst see, when the wrong-doers are brought up before their Lord, how they cast the blame one to another; how those who were despised (in the earth) say unto those who were proud: But for you, we should have been believers

34:32.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُوٓاْ أَنَحۡنُ صَدَدۡنَٰكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَكُمۖ بَلۡ كُنتُم مُّجۡرِمِينَ
34:32.en: Those who were proud say unto those who were despised: Did we drive you away from the guidance after it had come unto you? Nay, but ye were guilty

34:33.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ بَلۡ مَكۡرُ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذۡ تَأۡمُرُونَنَآ أَن نَّكۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَنَجۡعَلَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادࣰ اۚ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ فِيٓ أَعۡنَاقِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۖ هَلۡ يُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
34:33.en: Those who were despised say unto those who were proud: Nay but (it was your) scheming night and day, when ye commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals unto Him. And they are filled with remorse when they behold the doom; and We place carcans on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they requited aught save what they used to do

34:34.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا فِي قَرۡيَةࣲ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتۡرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلۡتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
34:34.en: And We sent not unto any township a warner, but its pampered ones declared: Lo! we are disbelievers in that wherewith ye have been sent

34:35.ar: وَقَالُواْ نَحۡنُ أَكۡثَرُ أَمۡوَٰلࣰ ا وَأَوۡلَٰدࣰ ا وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
34:35.en: And they say: We are more (than you) in wealth and children. We are not the punished

34:36.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
34:36.en: Say (O Muhammad): Lo! my Lord enlargeth the provision for whom He will and narroweth it (for whom He will). But most of mankind know not

34:37.ar: وَمَآ أَمۡوَٰلُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُكُم بِٱلَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمۡ عِندَنَا زُلۡفَىٰٓ إِلَّا مَنۡ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ جَزَآءُ ٱلضِّعۡفِ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ وَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡغُرُفَٰتِ ءَامِنُونَ
34:37.en: And it is not your wealth nor your children that will bring you near unto Us, but he who believeth and doeth good (he draweth near). As for such, theirs will be twofold reward for what they did and they will dwell secure in lofty halls

34:38.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡعَوۡنَ فِيٓ ءَايَٰتِنَا مُعَٰجِزِينَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ مُحۡضَرُونَ
34:38.en: And as for those who strive against Our revelations, challenging, they will be brought to the doom

34:39.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُ لَهُۥۚ وَمَآ أَنفَقۡتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَهُوَ يُخۡلِفُهُۥۖ وَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
34:39.en: Say: Lo! my Lord enlargeth the provision for whom He will of His bondmen, and narroweth (it) for him. And whatsoever ye spend (for good) He replaceth it. And He is the Best of Providers

7:99.ar: أَفَأَمِنُواْ مَكۡرَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَلَا يَأۡمَنُ مَكۡرَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
7:99.en: Are they then secure from Allah's scheme? None deemeth himself secure from Allah's scheme save folk that perish

53:39.ar: وَأَن لَّيۡسَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
53:39.en: And that man hath only that for which he maketh effort

2:276.ar: يَمۡحَقُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْ وَيُرۡبِي ٱلصَّدَقَٰتِۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ أَثِيمٍ
2:276.en: Allah hath blighted usury and made almsgiving fruitful. Allah loveth not the impious and guilty

oD7gkMJ9Mdo.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 8: Wealth Is Not Proof of Allah's Love
oD7gkMJ9Mdo.one_line: Saba 34:34-39: the wealthy resist warners, but wealth and children are not proof of Allah's love; provision is a trust, safety is only in Jannah, and spending returns.
oD7gkMJ9Mdo.summary: He reminds the class that submission means giving up a cherished free will, and that its test comes only when our will differs from Allah's. Recapping earlier verses, he notes Muslims address opponents by letting results judge, and that followers cannot blame leaders for lies they chose to believe, which he illustrates with the wife of a drug lord who claimed not to know and the companions' wives who refused unlawful provision. Today we know too much about suffering to plead ignorance, which makes a strong community the first priority. In verses 34 to 37 the comfortable reject every warner and cite their wealth and children as proof they are right; the answer is that Allah widens and tightens provision as He wills, and only faith and fulfilling one's purpose bring nearness, with double reward for those who use wealth for Him. Real safety exists only in Paradise, so hold worldly things in the hand and not the heart. Verse 39 repeats the point to believers with one added word: Allah tightens provision for their own good, and on the Day of Judgment He may show what would have happened. He criticizes a community full of ideas but short on volunteers, explains sadaqah as proof of truthfulness, and urges everyone to invest in the community, trusting the best of providers.

outline.heading: Why study an overlooked surah
outline.gist: Saba is rarely explained, unlike popular surahs such as Al-Kahf, yet it is deep and vital for a community.

outline.heading: Submission means surrendering a cherished free will
outline.gist: Free will is the most precious human trait; Allah does not interfere with it until death, and Islam is choosing to give it to Him.

outline.heading: The test comes when wills differ
outline.gist: Agreeing with your father when you want the same thing proves nothing; obedience shows when your wishes clash with Allah's.

outline.heading: Recap: Dawud's kingdom and Saba
outline.gist: One society prospered through gratitude and sharing, the other failed.

outline.heading: Either we or you are rightly guided
outline.gist: Muslims tell opponents to let time judge; each side answers for its own deeds, and a community following revelation should prove itself by results.

outline.heading: Revealed to prepare for Madinah
outline.gist: The passage came just before the hijrah to teach the Prophet how to build a community, far from today's reality.

outline.heading: Leaders and followers blaming each other
outline.gist: No one is excused for following; you can consult and ask but you carry your own choices on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Choosing to believe convenient lies
outline.gist: Parents who believe their children's lies, and spouses and friends who do the same, are not excused when it all collapses.

outline.heading: The drug lord's wife and the companions' wives
outline.gist: Claiming ignorance of a husband's crimes is weak; companions' wives told their husbands not to bring them unlawful provision.

outline.heading: Too much knowledge to plead ignorance
outline.gist: We watch oppression in real time, cannot deliberately stay ignorant, and must decide how to act.

outline.heading: Build a strong community first
outline.gist: To help anyone else, Muslims must give up differences and biases and strengthen the unity of their own community.

outline.heading: The comfortable reject every warner
outline.gist: Those benefiting from the status quo reject warners and cite their wealth and children as proof they will not be punished.

outline.heading: Economy and the cycle of easy times
outline.gist: People care about who governs only when prices rise; too much wealth made Muslims abandon politics.

outline.heading: Two nearly identical verses, two audiences
outline.gist: The repeated verse answers first those resisting change, then those wanting it.

outline.heading: First answer: provision is Allah's choice
outline.gist: Wealth comes and goes by Allah's will; using success as proof of being right or loved is arrogance.

outline.heading: Only faith and fulfilling your purpose bring nearness
outline.gist: Wealth and children help only when used for Allah; then they earn a double reward.

outline.heading: The poor companions and the dhikr after prayer
outline.gist: The poor feared the rich would take all the reward; the rich adopted the dhikr too, showing that more given means higher aims and deeper falls.

outline.heading: Know which side of the rope you are on
outline.gist: Most of us were given plenty and should raise youth to see what they have to use and be grateful for.

outline.heading: Safe in the high chambers: security only in Jannah
outline.gist: Nothing in this world is secure, health, job, wealth or status, which is why people seek safety in money and family.

outline.heading: Do not feel secure from Allah's plan
outline.gist: Enjoy blessings as a trust while remembering they can be taken, and worship Allah for who He is.

outline.heading: Too invested to walk away
outline.gist: Like a recruit drawn in by houses and cars, an invested heart cannot let go; the early generations kept the world in their hands only.

outline.heading: A question on barakah
outline.gist: Accountability grows with what you are given; barakah is provision serving its purpose, granted to those who follow Allah's way.

outline.heading: Recitation: those striving against Our signs
outline.gist: He recites the verse on those who try to frustrate Allah's signs.

outline.heading: What it means to strive against the signs
outline.gist: The phrase appears twice in the surah; the sign here is that wealth has nothing to do with being loved or right.

outline.heading: It is how you live, not what you say
outline.gist: You are judged by what you strive for even if you do not reach it.

outline.heading: Living to disprove the sign
outline.gist: Those who insist their success is their own doing and use wealth for themselves are brought to punishment.

outline.heading: A granted dua is not proof of love
outline.gist: The question is what you did with what you were given, and whether it had barakah.

outline.heading: We talk the talk but do not walk the walk
outline.gist: Everyone agrees on programs, such as for people with disabilities, but no one takes them on.

outline.heading: I do not need your ideas, I need your time
outline.gist: Good ideas already exist; the community lacks people with time and patience to implement them.

outline.heading: Second answer: addressed to His servants
outline.gist: Ibad usually refers to believers; this answer is for those who follow Him.

outline.heading: Tightened for their own sake
outline.gist: The added word shows Allah gives more or less for our long-term good, and may show us the alternate outcome on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Asking why a dua was not granted
outline.gist: Those who ask may be shown how the thing they wanted would have ruined them.

outline.heading: Dua shows Allah your plan
outline.gist: When you ask for good with a good intention you are rewarded for the plan, whether or not it is granted.

outline.heading: Whatever you spend: sadaqah as proof of truthfulness
outline.gist: Spending includes time, knowledge and emotion; sadaqah means evidence of sincerity, not charity.

33:70.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَقُولُواْ قَوۡلࣰ ا سَدِيدࣰ ا
33:70.en: O ye who believe! Guard your duty to Allah, and speak words straight to the point

33:71.ar: يُصۡلِحۡ لَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلَكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡۗ وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ فَازَ فَوۡزًا عَظِيمًا
33:71.en: He will adjust your works for you and will forgive you your sins. Whosoever obeyeth Allah and His messenger, he verily hath gained a signal victory

33:72.ar: إِنَّا عَرَضۡنَا ٱلۡأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلۡجِبَالِ فَأَبَيۡنَ أَن يَحۡمِلۡنَهَا وَأَشۡفَقۡنَ مِنۡهَا وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ ظَلُومࣰ ا جَهُولࣰ ا
33:72.en: Lo! We offered the trust unto the heavens and the earth and the hills, but they shrank from bearing it and were afraid of it. And man assumed it. Lo! he hath proved a tyrant and a fool

33:73.ar: لِّيُعَذِّبَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكَٰتِ وَيَتُوبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمَۢا
33:73.en: So Allah punisheth hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and idolatrous men and idolatrous women. But Allah pardoneth believing men and believing women, and Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

33:22.ar: وَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابَ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥۚ وَمَا زَادَهُمۡ إِلَّآ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَتَسۡلِيمࣰ ا
33:22.en: And when the true believers saw the clans, they said: This is that which Allah and His messenger promised us. Allah and His messenger are true. It did but confirm them in their faith and resignation

33:35.ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ وَٱلۡمُسۡلِمَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتِينَ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَٱلصَّٰبِرَٰتِ وَٱلۡخَٰشِعِينَ وَٱلۡخَٰشِعَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقِينَ وَٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمِينَ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمَٰتِ وَٱلۡحَٰفِظِينَ فُرُوجَهُمۡ وَٱلۡحَٰفِظَٰتِ وَٱلذَّٰكِرِينَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَٱلذَّٰكِرَٰتِ أَعَدَّ ٱللَّهُ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣰ وَأَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
33:35.en: Lo! men who surrender unto Allah, and women who surrender, and men who believe and women who believe, and men who obey and women who obey, and men who speak the truth and women who speak the truth, and men who persevere (in righteousness) and women who persevere, and men who are humble and women who are humble, and men who give alms and women who give alms, and men who fast and women who fast, and men who guard their modesty and women who guard (their modesty), and men who remember Allah much and women who remember - Allah hath prepared for them forgiveness and a vast reward

22:18.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسۡجُدُۤ لَهُۥۤ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلشَّمۡسُ وَٱلۡقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلۡجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِۖ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُۗ وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكۡرِمٍۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفۡعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ۩
22:18.en: Hast thou not seen that unto Allah payeth adoration whosoever is in the heavens and whosoever is in the earth, and the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and the hills, and the trees, and the beasts, and many of mankind, while there are many unto whom the doom is justly due. He whom Allah scorneth, there is none to give him honour. Lo! Allah doeth what He will

17:44.ar: تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ ٱلسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّۚ وَإِن مِّن شَيۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورࣰ ا
17:44.en: The seven heavens and the earth and all that is therein praise Him, and there is not a thing but hymneth His praise; but ye understand not their praise. Lo! He is ever Clement, Forgiving

33:8.ar: لِّيَسۡـَٔلَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ عَن صِدۡقِهِمۡۚ وَأَعَدَّ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
33:8.en: That He may ask the loyal of their loyalty. And He hath prepared a painful doom for the unfaithful
