JKGx4F2NAMw.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 20: Review of the Surah, Words That Hit the Mark, and the Trust (33:70-73)
JKGx4F2NAMw.one_line: A review of Al-Ahzab as a surah of hard obedience, then speaking words that achieve their goal, and the trust of free choice.
JKGx4F2NAMw.summary: He states his aim: to teach how to approach the Quran, reading each surah as a unit within a cluster revealed in response to events. He reviews Al-Ahzab as the surah of obeying Allah when it is hardest: telling adopted children the truth, fear at the Trench, the judgment on Qurayzah, the wives choosing a simple life, women's conduct and equality, the marriage to Zaynab, the rulings specific to the Prophet, the etiquette of his home and the jilbab, all anchored in 33:36. If a command causes distress, either you are doing it wrong or looking at it wrongly, and dhikr is the remedy. In 33:70-71 taqwa is prevention, and qawl sadid is speech that hits its target: correct people in the way most likely to help them, usually gently, not to relieve your own anger. He warns against advising strangers and admits that yelling at his own child served him, not the child. In 33:72 the trust offered to heavens, earth and mountains, which they feared, is the freedom to choose obedience; every other creature follows its nature, while humans can refuse even food when hungry. People will be judged on how they used this trust, the hypocrites punished and believers granted repentance, so trust that His commands bring ease. He ends with Ibn Ata'illah: strive fully, then accept what is decreed without blaming yourself.

outline.heading: His goal: learning how to approach the Quran
outline.gist: Not just explaining verses but reading each surah as a unit with a topic, connected to others with the same theme.

outline.heading: Revealed in response to events, in clusters
outline.gist: Stripped of the events they addressed, verses become obscure; surahs come in groups of three to five that study one topic from several angles.

outline.heading: Submission is multi-dimensional
outline.gist: Finding obedience hard is normal; what marks a Muslim is the will to submit, then a lifelong struggle to do it; Al-Ahzab is the key to its cluster.

outline.heading: Review: the four opening commands
outline.gist: Have taqwa as prevention, do not follow the disbelievers and hypocrites, follow what is revealed, and rely on Allah when you cannot see the end.

outline.heading: Review: the adopted child must know
outline.gist: Raise an orphan with love but never give him your name or hide that he is not biologically yours; living a lie is worse than the hurt of truth.

outline.heading: Review: fear at the Trench
outline.gist: Ten thousand Confederates against Madinah; the surah dissects how hypocrites called the promise a lie and urged people home.

outline.heading: Review: the believers' response
outline.gist: Seeing the Confederates, the believers said this is what Allah promised, and it only increased their faith.

outline.heading: Review: Banu Qurayzah
outline.gist: Their treason in war led to the execution of the men involved and expulsion of the rest, a hard judgment the surah records.

outline.heading: Review: the wives' choice of a simple life
outline.gist: He chose to live simply while any Muslim was in need; when his wives asked for more, they were offered a graceful release or a life with him as it was, and all chose him.

outline.heading: A conversation no marriage finds easy
outline.gist: Telling a wife this is as much as we will ever have, by choice, is hard; that is why it is an example of submission.

outline.heading: Review: women's conduct and equality
outline.gist: Rules on dress and speech, and the verse listing believing men and women equally in every act of worship, each hard for a different generation.

outline.heading: The foundation verse: 33:36
outline.gist: Whether you like it, find it easy or fit it into your plans does not matter; we are not Allah's partners, He commands and we obey.

outline.heading: Review: the command to marry Zaynab
outline.gist: Lawful because Zayd was not his son, yet he feared the rumour would smear Islam; Allah told him He had more right to be feared, a verse no impostor would recite.

outline.heading: If you feel distress, check yourself
outline.gist: The deen was not sent to distress you; either you are doing it wrong and should ask someone knowledgeable, or you are looking at it wrongly.

outline.heading: Review: dhikr as the remedy
outline.gist: 300 phrases morning and evening take about five minutes and can grow; and asking before every decision whether Allah would approve makes commands easier.

outline.heading: Review: what was permitted, then forbidden, to him
outline.gist: He was allowed any number of wives but married only those Allah commanded; then he was forbidden to marry more, and accepted that too.

outline.heading: Review: guests in his home and the screen
outline.gist: Imagine the queue after every prayer; guests lingered for conversation in a one-room house, and Allah, not shy of the truth, told them to eat and leave.

outline.heading: Review: why we send salawat on him
outline.gist: After so much of his private life was exposed, the command to bless him shows none of it lowers his status; we learn from his difficulties.

outline.heading: Review: the jilbab
outline.gist: Perhaps harder to discuss today than ever; a true believer may struggle with it but still does it.

outline.heading: Taqwa as prevention
outline.gist: Taqwa is never entering the harm in the first place, unlike repentance after it, as preventing diabetes beats curing it.

outline.heading: Qawl sadid: words that hit the target
outline.gist: Sadid is speech that achieves its purpose; not always tender, but never said for your own status or to feel righteous.

outline.heading: Correcting a brother's mistake
outline.gist: The wrong must be named, but how you say it can help him improve or make him defend it to the end of his life.

outline.heading: Gentleness beautifies, and the rare exception
outline.gist: Gentleness adorns whatever it touches; once the Prophet grabbed Umar by the collar because that suited Umar, one case in thousands.

outline.heading: Your deeds perfected and sins forgiven
outline.gist: People hate being told they are wrong, so preserve their dignity; when you speak this way, Allah perfects your deeds and forgives your sins.

outline.heading: Religion is sincere advice
outline.gist: Nasihah is central but sensitive; given badly, it can turn someone into an activist for the very mistake you meant to correct.

outline.heading: Do not advise people you do not know
outline.gist: Without knowing someone's mindset you will likely get it wrong; unless you are their imam, let someone close to them speak; a younger sibling deserves thought first.

outline.heading: The urge to be harsh
outline.gist: With a sibling or child the instinct is to yell or threaten; there are many better ways, none of them satisfying to you.

outline.heading: Yelling serves you, not the child
outline.gist: When his two-year-old son broke something, yelling relieved his own stress and taught nothing; pretending it was for the child adds a lie to the sin.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:72-73
outline.gist: He recites the final two verses of the surah.

outline.heading: What is the trust?
outline.gist: Commentators differ so widely that no majority view exists; Allah left it unnamed for a reason.

outline.heading: Offered to heavens, earth and mountains
outline.gist: The greatest things a human can see refused it out of fear, not reluctance; the human carried it and has been unjust and ignorant with it.

outline.heading: The trust is the choice to obey
outline.gist: Read in light of the surah, the trust is the critical ability to obey or refuse, and it counts most when obedience is hard.

outline.heading: Everything else follows its laws
outline.gist: Planets, stars and galaxies never deviate, which is why science works; no ostrich wonders why it was created and no tiger needs a purpose.

outline.heading: The hungry animal always eats
outline.gist: A healthy, hungry animal always eats; a fasting human refuses the food he craves by choice.

outline.heading: The one noise in the symphony
outline.gist: Everything glorifies Allah and prostrates to Him; in a narration the sky, mountains, earth and seas ask permission to destroy disobedient humans.

outline.heading: How are you doing with the trust?
outline.gist: Are you mostly choosing well, returning quickly after mistakes, accepting commands you struggle with, or making the haram halal?

outline.heading: The trust above all trusts
outline.gist: You are entrusted with health, wealth, family and work, but the trust is the choice to say yes to Allah; on the Day of Judgment you will be asked what you did with it.

outline.heading: When the white flag went up
outline.gist: Facing your record, every time you took what you should not, ran away, feared people or chose ease will be laid against the trust.

outline.heading: So that Allah may punish and ask the truthful
outline.gist: The trust makes punishment just; it echoes 33:8, the pledge taken so the truthful could be asked about their truth.

outline.heading: Repentance for the believers
outline.gist: Mistakes are part of the deal; treat the trust with respect, return to Him when you slip, and He grants repentance; no one else carries your consequences.

outline.heading: People blaming each other
outline.gist: On that day people will turn on friends and family asking why they did not remind them; no one will be wronged.

outline.heading: What Al-Ahzab teaches
outline.gist: There is never an option once Allah commands; if it feels hard, look at it differently and remember Him, because His commands exist to bring you ease, which you may see only years later.

outline.heading: Returning the trust
outline.gist: When your limbs testify, the choice is taken back and you are evaluated on how you used it.

outline.heading: Good news and justice
outline.gist: Strive and He grants repentance and a second life of joy; fail and we will not even object to the justice of punishment.

outline.heading: Outro
Ibn Ata'illah: resolve cannot pierce destiny
outline.gist: Building on the balance of means and devotion: strive with full energy for a correct goal, knowing that effort may not change what is decreed.

outline.heading: Do not blame yourself
outline.gist: If it was not decreed, no effort would have brought it; accept and move on, and you will live happier and more productively.

34:10.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا دَاوُۥدَ مِنَّا فَضۡلࣰ اۖ يَٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُۥ وَٱلطَّيۡرَۖ وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلۡحَدِيدَ
34:10.en: And assuredly We gave David grace from Us, (saying): O ye hills and birds, echo his psalms of praise! And We made the iron supple unto him

34:11.ar: أَنِ ٱعۡمَلۡ سَٰبِغَٰتࣲ وَقَدِّرۡ فِي ٱلسَّرۡدِۖ وَٱعۡمَلُواْ صَٰلِحًاۖ إِنِّي بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
34:11.en: Saying: Make thou long coats of mail and measure the links (thereof). And do ye right. Lo! I am Seer of what ye do

34:12.ar: وَلِسُلَيۡمَٰنَ ٱلرِّيحَ غُدُوُّهَا شَهۡرࣱ وَرَوَاحُهَا شَهۡرࣱۖ وَأَسَلۡنَا لَهُۥ عَيۡنَ ٱلۡقِطۡرِۖ وَمِنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ مَن يَعۡمَلُ بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ بِإِذۡنِ رَبِّهِۦۖ وَمَن يَزِغۡ مِنۡهُمۡ عَنۡ أَمۡرِنَا نُذِقۡهُ مِنۡ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
34:12.en: And unto Solomon (We gave) the wind, whereof the morning course was a month's journey and the evening course a month's journey, and We caused the fount of copper to gush forth for him, and (We gave him) certain of the jinn who worked before him by permission of his Lord. And such of them as deviated from Our command, them We caused to taste the punishment of flaming Fire

38:26.ar: يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةࣰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدُۢ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
38:26.en: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

18:96.ar: ءَاتُونِي زُبَرَ ٱلۡحَدِيدِۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيۡنَ ٱلصَّدَفَيۡنِ قَالَ ٱنفُخُواْۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَعَلَهُۥ نَارࣰ ا قَالَ ءَاتُونِيٓ أُفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡهِ قِطۡرࣰ ا
18:96.en: Give me pieces of iron - till, when he had levelled up (the gap) between the cliffs, he said: Blow! - till, when he had made it a fire, he said: Bring me molten copper to pour thereon

7XRQ2a769a8.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 2: Dawud and Sulayman, a Society Built on Faith
7XRQ2a769a8.one_line: Saba 34:10-12: Dawud and Sulayman as a model society whose nucleus is faith, completed by knowledge, roles, organization and centralization.
7XRQ2a769a8.summary: He recaps the surah's angle on submission: whole societies, not only individuals, must build on faith, yet faith alone does not make a civilization thrive. Before reading the passage he presses a hard question: Muslims in Canada are a population, not a community, because nothing is centralized, neither religious, social, financial nor political leadership, and so youth find nothing to belong to and little planned in London has been achieved in five years. He then explains verses 10 to 12. Dawud was given bounty: mountains and birds responding to his glorification, a sign of a person in harmony with creation. He was the first called khalifa in the Quran and played more roles than any prophet besides Muhammad, which required discipline and organization; we will be asked whether we fulfilled the roles our opportunities allowed. Iron made pliable points to real science, chain mail that changed warfare, and to the duty to use any advantage for good. Sulayman continued the kingdom because its elements were in place: knowledge of the seasonal winds for trade, molten copper, and jinn working for him. He ends by contrasting this with Muslim cultures that use jinn as superstition and blame them for illness and failure.

outline.heading: Recap: societies must submit to Allah too
outline.gist: The cluster of surahs on submission; Saba looks at it from the angle of whole societies, which need faith alongside justice, economy and vision.

outline.heading: Faith as the nucleus, not the only element
outline.gist: Dawud and Sulayman show a society built on faith plus much more; Muslim-majority societies have Islam as culture but do not build on it.

outline.heading: Are we a community or a minority?
outline.gist: Without centralized religious, social, financial or political leadership, Muslims in Canada are scattered populations rather than a community.

outline.heading: Centralization gives youth something to belong to
outline.gist: Any form of centralization creates representation; without it young people drift to other groups and return late and lost.

outline.heading: Five years with no planned milestone
outline.gist: Little planned in the London community has been achieved; the problem is not space but people not feeling part of something.

outline.heading: Two examples: Dawud's kingdom and Saba
outline.gist: The surah gives an uplifting model and a failing one; the surah is named after the failure because that is the danger.

outline.heading: Reading the passage: recitation rules
outline.gist: He recites the opening verses and explains how to pronounce certain letters in them.

outline.heading: Al-Basir: Allah sees what is done in public
outline.gist: The difference between Khabir, Sami' and Basir; Basir concerns visible actions that affect others, which is where a society should intervene.

outline.heading: Fadl: bounty beyond what is deserved
outline.gist: Fadl is something extra given out of generosity, above the baseline of mercy and justice.

outline.heading: Awwibi: mountains, echo back with him
outline.gist: Allah addresses the mountains directly; the word means to return or echo what is recited.

outline.heading: Dawud's recitation and Abu Musa's voice
outline.gist: Dawud was the first prophet given a scripture with a method of recitation; the Prophet praised Abu Musa al-Ash'ari's voice as one of Dawud's pipes.

outline.heading: Harmony with creation
outline.gist: Two readings of the mountains and birds responding; either way, following revelation puts a person in harmony with a universe that glorifies Allah.

outline.heading: Dawud, the first called khalifa
outline.gist: The word khalifa first appeared attached to Dawud, presenting the human being positively as a responsible agent, not a punished sinner.

outline.heading: Dawud's many roles and fulfilling ours
outline.gist: Prophet, king, judge, commander, artist, inventor and family man; being a khalifa means fulfilling the roles you are given to their full potential.

outline.heading: Dawud's fast and night prayer: an organized life
outline.gist: The Prophet named Dawud's fasting and night prayer the most beloved; playing so many roles required discipline and time management.

outline.heading: Why Dawud is the clearest model of khilafah
outline.gist: Other prophets lacked some roles; Dawud and Muhammad had the fullest range.

outline.heading: Opportunity and broadening your horizons
outline.gist: Roles depend on opportunity; those given much will be asked why they did not play more roles, so the young should learn widely.

outline.heading: Two percent can change a society
outline.gist: A small committed core of multi-role individuals is enough to move the rest of a community.

outline.heading: How Muslims view Dawud versus biblical accounts
outline.gist: Islam sees Dawud as an upright prophet, not the morally compromised figure of later accounts.

outline.heading: Iron made pliable: real science
outline.gist: Softening iron means Dawud learned metallurgy, knowledge others did not have.

outline.heading: Coats of mail and measured links
outline.gist: Sard is precise knitting of links; chain mail replaced heavy plate and changed warfare.

outline.heading: Civilizations that kept knowledge
outline.gist: Early Muslims gathered and translated the knowledge of other peoples instead of burning it, which later fed Europe's advance.

outline.heading: Work righteousness: using advantage for good
outline.gist: An edge in power or knowledge raises the obligation to do good, not to oppress or sell more weapons.

outline.heading: Faith connects all the elements
outline.gist: Dawud's civilization differed because faith tied its knowledge and power to a good purpose.

outline.heading: Sulayman and the wind: reading the verse
outline.gist: Recitation notes on the verse, including where a reciter may stop either way.

outline.heading: Continuity: Sulayman inherits a working kingdom
outline.gist: Because the elements were in place, the kingdom outlived Dawud, as Islam spread across three continents after the Prophet.

outline.heading: The wind as knowledge of seasonal currents
outline.gist: Sulayman understood the monthly wind patterns, used them for fleets and trade, and grew rich and strong.

outline.heading: A spring of molten copper
outline.gist: Sulayman went a step further than his father in metallurgy; Dhul-Qarnayn later used the same science.

outline.heading: Jinn working by Allah's permission
outline.gist: Jinn served Sulayman by Allah's leave, and those who defied the command are threatened with punishment; he asks what the symbolism is.

outline.heading: How Muslims misuse jinn today
outline.gist: Jinn become an excuse for failure, sickness and psychiatric illness, sometimes leading to abuse of the mentally ill.

outline.heading: A superstitious culture, not a prophetic one
outline.gist: Sulayman used the jinn to move forward; Muslims have become superstitious, as in a childhood memory of a house being cleansed of spirits.

33:56.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّۚ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ صَلُّواْ عَلَيۡهِ وَسَلِّمُواْ تَسۡلِيمًا
33:56.en: Lo! Allah and His angels shower blessings on the Prophet. O ye who believe! Ask blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation

33:57.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡذُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا مُّهِينࣰ ا
33:57.en: Lo! those who malign Allah and His messenger, Allah hath cursed them in the world and the Hereafter, and hath prepared for them the doom of the disdained

33:58.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡذُونَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ مَا ٱكۡتَسَبُواْ فَقَدِ ٱحۡتَمَلُواْ بُهۡتَٰنࣰ ا وَإِثۡمࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:58.en: And those who malign believing men and believing women undeservedly, they bear the guilt of slander and manifest sin

33:59.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ وَبَنَاتِكَ وَنِسَآءِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يُدۡنِينَ عَلَيۡهِنَّ مِن جَلَٰبِيبِهِنَّۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَن يُعۡرَفۡنَ فَلَا يُؤۡذَيۡنَۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
33:59.en: O Prophet! Tell thy wives and thy daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks close round them (when they go abroad). That will be better, so that they may be recognised and not annoyed. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

33:21.ar: لَّقَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ فِي رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةࣱ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلۡيَوۡمَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَ وَذَكَرَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا
33:21.en: Verily in the messenger of Allah ye have a good example for him who looketh unto Allah and the Last Day, and remembereth Allah much

33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled

33:43.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتُهُۥ لِيُخۡرِجَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِۚ وَكَانَ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رَحِيمࣰ ا
33:43.en: He it is Who blesseth you, and His angels (bless you), that He may bring you forth from darkness unto light; and He is ever Merciful to the believers

40:7.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَحۡمِلُونَ ٱلۡعَرۡشَ وَمَنۡ حَوۡلَهُۥ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَيُؤۡمِنُونَ بِهِۦ وَيَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۖ رَبَّنَا وَسِعۡتَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲ رَّحۡمَةࣰ وَعِلۡمࣰ ا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ سَبِيلَكَ وَقِهِمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
40:7.en: Those who bear the Throne, and all who are round about it, hymn the praises of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who believe (saying): Our Lord! Thou comprehendest all things in mercy and knowledge, therefor forgive those who repent and follow Thy way. Ward off from them the punishment of hell

16:123.ar: ثُمَّ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ أَنِ ٱتَّبِعۡ مِلَّةَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفࣰ اۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
16:123.en: And afterward We inspired thee (Muhammad, saying): Follow the religion of Abraham, as one by nature upright. He was not of the idolaters

6:108.ar: وَلَا تَسُبُّواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَسُبُّواْ ٱللَّهَ عَدۡوَۢا بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲۗ كَذَٰلِكَ زَيَّنَّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِم مَّرۡجِعُهُمۡ فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
6:108.en: Revile not those unto whom they pray beside Allah lest they wrongfully revile Allah through ignorance. Thus unto every nation have We made their deed seem fair. Then unto their Lord is their return, and He will tell them what they used to do

24:31.ar: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ

kCYS56SWEHY.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 18: Salawat on the Prophet, the Sin of Harm, and the Jilbab (33:56-59)
kCYS56SWEHY.one_line: Why the Friday verse of salawat sits where it does, what sending blessings and submitting to the Prophet mean, the gravity of harm, and the jilbab.
kCYS56SWEHY.summary: He argues that reading a surah by its theme gives you a compass, and shows it with 33:56, recited every Friday but rarely understood in place. Every story in Al-Ahzab has the Prophet at its centre as the example of obeying Allah under hardship, and his consistency is so complete that we forget what he endured, such as raising seven children after Khadijah died or enduring guests in silence. The verse is a remedy like the earlier command of dhikr: salah means connection, so we send blessings on him verbally, ideally in the Ibrahimi form and a daily count, and also connect by learning and living his way; blessings on the tongue with bad conduct at home are empty. Taslim here means handing over your own ways in submission, and we follow him because Allah chose him as the complete example. 33:57-58 warn that harming Allah and His Messenger, which includes bringing disrepute on Islam, and harming believers through slander are grave; he names two red lines, shirk and harm, because wronged people must forgive you themselves. 33:59 commands believing women to wear the jilbab, so they are known and less harassed; he explains hijab, khimar and jilbab, notes scholarly agreement on covering, and urges men in Canada to leave hijab advice to women.

outline.heading: Opening
Reading by theme gives you a compass
outline.gist: Knowing a surah's theme and cluster lets you interact with its verses instead of making wrong assumptions.

outline.heading: Obedience counts most when it is hard
outline.gist: Obeying when it is easy is self-serving; the whole surah builds towards 33:56, the verse imams recite every Friday that we have grown numb to.

outline.heading: The verse in its setting
outline.gist: It follows the Trench, the wives, Zaynab and the rulings on his home, just as the verses on his status followed the earlier stories.

outline.heading: An unparalleled verse
outline.gist: Nowhere else does Allah tell us something He Himself does for the Prophet; our daily salawat traces back to here.

outline.heading: Salawat as a remedy, like dhikr
outline.gist: Hardship comes financially, physically, socially and personally; just as dhikr irons out distress, salawat is singled out as a special form of it.

outline.heading: Words and practice
outline.gist: Like dhikr, salawat has a spoken form and a lived form.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:56-58
outline.gist: He recites the verses, noting the doubled ya in an-nabiyy when stopping.

outline.heading: He is at the centre of every story
outline.gist: Unlike surahs whose stories are remote from him, every story here involves the Prophet as the example of submitting under hardship, hence 33:21.

outline.heading: You know someone only in hard times
outline.gist: Anyone performs well in their prime; these stories show him under fear, poverty, social backlash and personal strain.

outline.heading: His consistency hides his circumstances
outline.gist: We ask about circumstances only when people fail; a co-worker who always performs is never asked, so we forget what he carried.

outline.heading: Why the Zaynab story is told
outline.gist: No one keeps the same character on every bad day; the story is there to show a human given a hard command who kept his mission.

outline.heading: A single father of seven
outline.gist: When Khadijah died he had seven children in his house, several not his own, and still carried the message as if nothing had changed.

outline.heading: No one knew his discomfort
outline.gist: Guests thought he enjoyed their hours-long visits until revelation exposed it.

outline.heading: Allah and His angels bless the Prophet
outline.gist: The verse mirrors 33:43, where Allah and His angels bless those who remember Him.

outline.heading: Ubayy: all my prayer for you
outline.gist: Asked how much of his prayer to devote to salawat, the Prophet kept saying more is better, until Ubayy said all of it and was promised relief from worry and forgiveness.

outline.heading: Worry and sadness
outline.gist: Hamm is anxiety from a burden you carry; huzn is sadness for any reason; salawat brings particular relief in our times.

outline.heading: Salah means connection
outline.gist: Allah's salah is mercy and support, the angels' is prayer for forgiveness as in 40:7; salah is the umbrella word for every kind of relationship with Allah, from the root of silah.

outline.heading: Strengthening the bond with him
outline.gist: Allah and His angels strengthen their bond with the Prophet, and the believers are commanded to do the same.

outline.heading: A command to every believer
outline.gist: Earlier commands in the surah concerned people of that time; this one addresses all believers, best done in the Ibrahimi form taught in prayer.

outline.heading: Salawat carries the most barakah
outline.gist: Add 100 or 200 salawat a day to the daily wird; of all forms he has tried, it brings the most blessing because you ask Allah to honour His beloved.

outline.heading: Start small
outline.gist: If 100 is too many, do ten after each prayer or after fajr and maghrib.

outline.heading: The second way: knowing and living his life
outline.gist: Learn the Quran he practised first and his sunnah, and adopt his values and lifestyle.

outline.heading: Salawat with no likeness to him is empty
outline.gist: Saying salawat all day while treating your wife and children without respect or love is a disconnect; the aim is the heart and behaviour.

outline.heading: Taslim: hand over your ways
outline.gist: Here it is not giving salam but submitting: give up the views and habits you held and take his way instead.

outline.heading: Because Allah chose him
outline.gist: We follow him because Allah blessed him first and made him the example; complex life needs at least one good example.

outline.heading: The most complete example
outline.gist: Isa is not seen as husband or leader, Musa spent his life in conflict, Sulayman and Dawud never struggled for food; Muhammad lived every role, and Ibrahim was his model.

outline.heading: Unless you think you are better
outline.gist: If Allah and His angels do this, believers have no reason not to, and taslim is what is asked of us alone.

outline.heading: Remember him at the Trench
outline.gist: Carrying earth for hours, keeping hopes up as Qurayzah broke its treaty, standing in long supplication.

outline.heading: He chose to come home empty-handed
outline.gist: He did not enjoy poverty; he chose it so no one could say he did it for wealth, and his own household complained.

outline.heading: Holding his character through it all
outline.gist: Gossip about Aisha, the command to marry Zaynab, guests who never left: he maintained his manners and mission through every day of it.

outline.heading: Our part: verbally and practically
outline.gist: Send blessings on him with the tongue, then live his way and submit to it.

outline.heading: Those who harm Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: Allah cannot be harmed; the phrase means harming people and His deen, and the Prophet was harmed by slander over Zaynab and Safiyyah and by overstaying guests.

outline.heading: Harm can be indirect
outline.gist: Conduct that gets labelled as Muslim and brings Islam into disrepute brings harm onto the Prophet's message.

outline.heading: Do not curse their idols
outline.gist: 6:108 forbids insulting others' gods lest they insult Allah, and the hadith counts causing your parents to be cursed as cursing them.

outline.heading: Every verse can apply to me
outline.gist: Never read a warning thinking it is about someone else; your behaviour brings benefit or harm to Allah's deen.

outline.heading: Harming believers without cause: buhtan
outline.gist: Ghibah is speaking of a fault someone really has; buhtan is inventing one, as with the slander of Aisha; both are clear sin.

outline.heading: Two red lines: shirk and harm
outline.gist: Understand tawhid well enough to keep it, and never harm people directly or indirectly; you may fail to do good, but do not do harm.

outline.heading: If you can do nothing else, do no harm
outline.gist: The hadith of charity due from everyone: enjoin good, then smile, and if you cannot even do that, withhold your harm.

outline.heading: The man who never smiled
outline.gist: A friend's father, kind and generous, never once smiled; some people lack even that, but anyone can refrain from harm.

outline.heading: Harm leaves you on your own
outline.gist: No scholar can tell you Allah has forgiven a wrong done to someone; only the person can forgive, and the harm holds people back on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:59: wives, daughters and believing women
outline.gist: After the screen specific to his wives, this command extends to all believing women.

outline.heading: Hijab, khimar and jilbab
outline.gist: Hijab is the umbrella concept of a barrier for both genders; khimar covers head and chest as in 24:31; jilbab is a fuller garment over head and body.

outline.heading: Known, and so not harassed
outline.gist: Dress is a statement of piety, as his own appearance means no woman has ever approached him; it attracts some prejudice but keeps away unwanted advances.

outline.heading: The harm you accept for Allah
outline.gist: Discrimination for looking Muslim earns reward and echoes what the companions faced; the harassment the verse speaks of becomes far less likely.

outline.heading: What scholars agree women cover
outline.gist: All four schools agree on covering everything but face and hands, differing only on the feet; any cloth or colour that fulfils the concept will do.

outline.heading: Men should not preach hijab
outline.gist: It has become an identity battle that harms people; Muslim men who do not bear it should leave the advice to women and focus on what young men struggle with.

outline.heading: Gender-sensitive teaching in Canada
outline.gist: These issues are delicate in Canadian society; address them sensitively without giving up the fundamentals.

outline.heading: It does not have to be comfortable
outline.gist: The surah's point: the command need not be easy, but we find ways to help Muslim youth hold to it.

HAsryOdRMS4.speaker_note: first session of his Sunday Saba series, refers to his Ahzab sessions and to the local community
HAsryOdRMS4.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 1: Introduction, Praise, the Hereafter and Knowledge with Mercy
HAsryOdRMS4.one_line: Introduction to Saba as submission at the level of societies, then 34:1-2: praise as an attitude, belief in the hereafter, and knowledge joined with mercy.
HAsryOdRMS4.summary: He places Saba in a cluster of surahs about submission: Al-Ahzab looked at obedience at the personal level, Saba looks at whole societies, which need faith as well as justice, wealth and good management. Muslims see Islam as communal, which is why Jumuah matters so much; a Muslim who treats faith as purely private may find his grandchildren no longer pray, as mosques emptied in parts of the Middle East in the 1960s and 70s. He urges Muslims to carry their own causes, such as oppressed Chinese Muslims, instead of expecting others to. Verse 1 then sets the surah's first laws. Praise is an attitude: it makes a society see its strengths and build on them, it moves praise away from the self and so removes vanity and entitlement, and it extends thanks to people through whom good came. The hereafter must be part of the equation, because morality cannot be explained to the deprived without accountability; inner awareness of Allah works better than cameras. Verse 2 pairs knowledge with mercy, as the Quran does throughout, so the more one learns the more merciful one must become, especially as a parent and teacher. He closes with Ibn Ata'illah's fourth aphorism: plan, do your part, then stop worrying about what Allah has already arranged.

outline.heading: Where Saba sits: a Makki surah after Al-Ahzab
outline.gist: Al-Ahzab is late Madani; Saba is a mid-Makkan surah, deep but rarely studied.

outline.heading: Obedience to Allah is total, not relative
outline.gist: We obey people partially, but submitting to Allah means aligning our will entirely with His.

outline.heading: From personal obedience to societal obedience
outline.gist: Al-Ahzab personalized every example; Saba looks at two civilizations, Dawud's and Saba's, to show submission at a societal level.

outline.heading: Prosperous societies that still decline
outline.gist: Justice, wealth and management are needed, but societies without faith slowly decline.

outline.heading: Societies need faith as individuals do
outline.gist: Stripping a community of faith prepares it for destruction.

outline.heading: Islam is communal: the meaning of Jumuah
outline.gist: Muslims practise faith as a group, and faith-based communities expressing themselves safely benefits everyone.

outline.heading: Boxing faith in leads to lost generations
outline.gist: Distancing from the community shows up in children and grandchildren who no longer pray.

outline.heading: Common sense builds rules; faith must be taught
outline.gist: People can agree on equality and schools by reason, but faith needs revelation, and Muslims express it openly in daily speech.

outline.heading: Jumuah as the community's safety valve
outline.gist: When a community stops caring for Jumuah the battle is lost; mosques emptied in the Levant after colonialism and the fall of the caliphate.

outline.heading: The farmer called to make forty for Jumuah
outline.gist: His teacher's story of needing a fortieth man while a Muslim farmer kept ploughing; a later revival brought people back.

outline.heading: The structure of the surah and reading with a compass
outline.gist: An introduction of principles, two examples, then commentary; knowing the theme makes personal reading easier.

outline.heading: The five surahs that open with praise
outline.gist: Surahs beginning with al-hamdu lillah always carry a societal dimension, as Al-Fatihah is recited in the plural.

outline.heading: A Muslim is never alone
outline.gist: Even alone, a Muslim is connected to the ummah past and present.

outline.heading: Forgetting the Chinese Muslims
outline.gist: A woman reminded him of the suffering of a huge Muslim population he had never prayed for.

outline.heading: Why expect mainstream media to care?
outline.gist: Others look after their own issues; Muslims should build their own platforms for fairness.

outline.heading: An entitled generation
outline.gist: Earlier generations knew no one would do things for them; today we expect others to carry our causes.

outline.heading: Recitation of the opening verses
outline.gist: He recites the first two verses.

outline.heading: Praise at the heart of the Prophet's identity
outline.gist: Ahmad and Muhammad come from praise, and his intercession begins with praise no one has offered before.

outline.heading: Praise as an attitude against despair
outline.gist: A society that cannot see its blessings has nothing to build on; Muslims see both what they have and what they lack.

outline.heading: Saying alhamdulillah when asked how you are
outline.gist: Answering with praise forces you to find something good; the companions asked each other repeatedly to draw it out.

outline.heading: First effect: building on strengths
outline.gist: Personal and professional growth comes from perfecting your strengths before patching weaknesses.

outline.heading: Criticizing the community without despair
outline.gist: Because he sees the community's real strengths, criticism is meant to fix gaps, not to crush.

outline.heading: Second effect: redirecting praise away from the self
outline.gist: Children need praise to grow confident, then must learn they are not the centre of the universe.

outline.heading: Praise removes vanity and entitlement
outline.gist: Praising Allah for success keeps a person working harder; self-praise breeds expectation of titles and respect.

outline.heading: Societies that feel superior fall
outline.gist: Nations that credit themselves with all greatness decline within generations.

outline.heading: Thanking the people Allah sent to help you
outline.gist: Praise extends to those through whom good came, yet we quickly forget those who stood by us.

outline.heading: Boasting about help we gave
outline.gist: We exaggerate the help we gave others; the daily supplications all centre on the single word of praise.

outline.heading: Everything belongs to Him by creation
outline.gist: Allah is praised because He created everything with no partner or helper, not merely because He owns it.

outline.heading: Praise in the hereafter
outline.gist: Praise in the next life will be easy because truth will be plain; it should be the same in this life.

outline.heading: Second law: no society works without the hereafter
outline.gist: Fear of something keeps people from breaking the law, and fear of the law fades for many.

outline.heading: Explaining morals to the deprived
outline.gist: To someone abused and left behind, appeals to social order, values or prison mean nothing.

outline.heading: The race with uneven head starts
outline.gist: A video of students stepping forward by privilege shows why morality without accountability is easy only for the comfortable.

outline.heading: Better than all the cameras
outline.gist: An inner sense of Allah watching does what surveillance cannot; the verse adds the hereafter on purpose.

outline.heading: Al-Hakim, al-Khabir
outline.gist: Specific names under the umbrella of al-Alim; the All-Wise uses knowledge rightly and the All-Aware knows hidden intentions.

outline.heading: Third point: what enters and leaves the earth and sky
outline.gist: Allah knows all movement: the dead and seeds entering the earth, what comes out, what descends and the deeds that rise.

outline.heading: Knowledge always paired with mercy

34:24.ar: ۞قُلۡ مَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۖ وَإِنَّآ أَوۡ إِيَّاكُمۡ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
34:24.en: Say: Who giveth you provision from the sky and the earth? Say: Allah, Lo! we or you assuredly are rightly guided or in error manifest

34:25.ar: قُل لَّا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّآ أَجۡرَمۡنَا وَلَا نُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
34:25.en: Say: Ye will not be asked of what we committed, nor shall we be asked of what ye do

34:31.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَلَا بِٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِۗ وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ مَوۡقُوفُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ يَرۡجِعُ بَعۡضُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ يَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لَوۡلَآ أَنتُمۡ لَكُنَّا مُؤۡمِنِينَ
34:31.en: And those who disbelieve say: We believe not in this Qur'an nor in that which was before it; but oh, if thou couldst see, when the wrong-doers are brought up before their Lord, how they cast the blame one to another; how those who were despised (in the earth) say unto those who were proud: But for you, we should have been believers

34:32.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُوٓاْ أَنَحۡنُ صَدَدۡنَٰكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَكُمۖ بَلۡ كُنتُم مُّجۡرِمِينَ
34:32.en: Those who were proud say unto those who were despised: Did we drive you away from the guidance after it had come unto you? Nay, but ye were guilty

34:33.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ بَلۡ مَكۡرُ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذۡ تَأۡمُرُونَنَآ أَن نَّكۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَنَجۡعَلَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادࣰ اۚ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ فِيٓ أَعۡنَاقِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۖ هَلۡ يُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
34:33.en: Those who were despised say unto those who were proud: Nay but (it was your) scheming night and day, when ye commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals unto Him. And they are filled with remorse when they behold the doom; and We place carcans on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they requited aught save what they used to do

34:40.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يَحۡشُرُهُمۡ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ يَقُولُ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ أَهَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِيَّاكُمۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡبُدُونَ
34:40.en: And on the day when He will gather them all together, He will say unto the angels: Did these worship you

34:41.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا مِن دُونِهِمۖ بَلۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡبُدُونَ ٱلۡجِنَّۖ أَكۡثَرُهُم بِهِم مُّؤۡمِنُونَ
34:41.en: They will say: Be Thou Glorified. Thou (alone) art our Guardian, not them! Nay, but they worshipped the jinn; most of them were believers in them

34:42.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَا يَمۡلِكُ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضࣲ نَّفۡعࣰ ا وَلَا ضَرࣰّ ا وَنَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ ٱلَّتِي كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
34:42.en: That day ye will possess no use nor hurt one for another. And We shall say unto those who did wrong: Taste the doom of the Fire which ye used to deny

34:43.ar: وَإِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتࣲ قَالُواْ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا رَجُلࣱ يُرِيدُ أَن يَصُدَّكُمۡ عَمَّا كَانَ يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُكُمۡ وَقَالُواْ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ إِفۡكࣱ مُّفۡتَرࣰ ىۚ وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلۡحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمۡ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحۡرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
34:43.en: And if Our revelations are recited unto them in plain terms, they say: This is naught else than a man who would turn you away from what your fathers used to worship; and they say: This is naught else than an invented lie. Those who disbelieve say of the truth when it reacheth them: This is naught else than mere magic

34:44.ar: وَمَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُم مِّن كُتُبࣲ يَدۡرُسُونَهَاۖ وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡهِمۡ قَبۡلَكَ مِن نَّذِيرࣲ‏
34:44.en: And We have given them no scriptures which they study, nor sent We unto them, before thee, any warner

34:45.ar: وَكَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَمَا بَلَغُواْ مِعۡشَارَ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمۡ فَكَذَّبُواْ رُسُلِيۖ فَكَيۡفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ
34:45.en: Those before them denied, and these have not attained a tithe of that which We bestowed on them (of old); yet they denied My messengers. How intense then was My abhorrence (of them)

6:151.ar: ۞قُلۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ أَتۡلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ أَلَّا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَوۡلَٰدَكُم مِّنۡ إِمۡلَٰقࣲ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُكُمۡ وَإِيَّاهُمۡۖ وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَا وَمَا بَطَنَۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُواْ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
6:151.en: Say: Come, I will recite unto you that which your Lord hath made a sacred duty for you: That ye ascribe no thing as partner unto Him and that ye do good to parents, and that ye slay not your children because of penury - We provide for you and for them - and that ye draw not nigh to lewd things whether open or concealed. And that ye slay not the life which Allah hath made sacred, save in the course of justice. This He hath command you, in order that ye may discern

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

5:116.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِيٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِحَقٍّۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُۥۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِي وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِكَۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
5:116.en: And when Allah saith: O Jesus, son of Mary! Didst thou say unto mankind: Take me and my mother for two gods beside Allah? he saith: Be glorified! It was not mine to utter that to which I had no right. If I used to say it, then Thou knewest it. Thou knowest what is in my mind, and I know not what is in Thy Mind. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower of Things Hidden

5:118.ar: إِن تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ عِبَادُكَۖ وَإِن تَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
5:118.en: If Thou punish them, lo! they are Thy slaves, and if Thou forgive them (lo! they are Thy slaves). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Mighty, the Wise

2:170.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَآ أَلۡفَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ
2:170.en: And when it is said unto them: Follow that which Allah hath revealed, they say: We follow that wherein we found our fathers. What! Even though their fathers were wholly unintelligent and had no guidance

24:11.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِٱلۡإِفۡكِ عُصۡبَةࣱ مِّنكُمۡۚ لَا تَحۡسَبُوهُ شَرࣰّ ا لَّكُمۖ بَلۡ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۚ لِكُلِّ ٱمۡرِيࣲٕ مِّنۡهُم مَّا ٱكۡتَسَبَ مِنَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِۚ وَٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبۡرَهُۥ مِنۡهُمۡ لَهُۥ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:11.en: Lo! they who spread the slander are a gang among you. Deem it not a bad thing for you; nay, it is good for you. Unto every man of them (will be paid) that which he hath earned of the sin; and as for him among them who had the greater share therein, his will be an awful doom

KLZLPNT8su4.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 9: The Angels Questioned and the Three Rejections
KLZLPNT8su4.one_line: Saba 34:40-45: the angels questioned about those who worshipped them, the duty to stop being followed blindly, and the three stock rejections of every reformer.
KLZLPNT8su4.summary: He opens by explaining why submission struck such a nerve in Arabia: the Arabs had no politics, wealth, social order or learning, only a fierce dignity and free will, which Islam asked them to hand to Allah. He stresses that each person owns and answers for his choices, then returns to his theme that local Muslims are a population, not a community, because nothing is centralized; politicians do not court them, youth lack belonging, and egos fill the masjid more than bodies, while leaders exist but few are willing to follow. In verses 40 to 42 Allah asks the angels whether people worshipped them; they panic and declare Him exalted, though they did nothing wrong. The lesson is for anyone who is followed: notice when people follow you blindly and stop it, as the Prophet did when his remark on pollinating palms was taken as a command, and as Umar did when Khalid was turning into a myth. Submitting to other than Allah wrongs one's own soul. Verses 43 to 45 list the three answers every reformer hears: it breaks our forefathers' ways, it is a fabrication, and it is magic or superstition. He calls for weighing tradition honestly and for fresh ideas, knowing they will meet the same pushback.

outline.heading: Submission is what makes Islam unique
outline.gist: Born Muslims rarely think about it, but the first Muslims had to answer whether they would give up their free will.

outline.heading: Arabia had no politics and no wealth
outline.gist: Thousands of splintering tribes and grinding poverty; infanticide came from fear of poverty more than hatred of girls.

outline.heading: Social and intellectual collapse
outline.gist: Cousin tribes killed each other, children and parents mistreated each other, and literacy was not valued.

outline.heading: All they had was dignity and free will
outline.gist: Never ruled because they were not worth conquering, the Arabs prized making their own decisions; by other measures a prophet from the Jewish tribes made more sense.

outline.heading: Asking them to surrender the one thing they owned
outline.gist: Submitting free will to Allah struck a nerve; once a believer chooses submission, a command of Allah leaves no option.

outline.heading: Recap: submission of societies so far
outline.gist: Dawud's grateful kingdom, Saba's failure, letting time judge between us, and followers who cannot blame leaders.

outline.heading: Your choices are sacred and you answer for them
outline.gist: Accepting accountability is the core of the deen; teach children that their choices are their only real possession.

outline.heading: The last paragraphs of the surah and what a society is
outline.gist: He previews the run of commands to say at the end of the surah and defines a society as a group that centralizes something.

outline.heading: Four kinds of centralization, none of them here
outline.gist: Politics, finances, religious leadership or social life; local Muslims have centralized none.

outline.heading: Push for one form of centralization
outline.gist: The same problems repeat generation after generation; families should discuss which of the possible forms to pursue.

outline.heading: Why politicians do not court Muslims
outline.gist: Without unity a large, young population gets no promises on food, housing contracts or schools.

outline.heading: Depriving the next generation
outline.gist: Lack of centralization denies our children dignity, belonging and identity.

outline.heading: The masjid is big enough for our bodies, not our egos
outline.gist: Sincerity and humility are needed to push those in positions to discuss options.

outline.heading: Chinatown and a common fund
outline.gist: Others centralize socially; Muslims already have a masjid and could at least pool money, the language of power.

outline.heading: Nothing changes for lack of trust
outline.gist: A cramped masjid and stalled projects show the problem is trust and centralization, not money or manpower.

outline.heading: Youth need a cause to belong to
outline.gist: Bored young men find something else to join; the Prophet drew people who wanted to change the world.

outline.heading: Leaders need people willing to be led
outline.gist: The best leader is the best follower of the Prophet; too many people wanting to lead ended the caliphate.

outline.heading: Recitation of verses 40 to 42
outline.gist: He notes that coordinating a community is far easier than fixing world politics, then recites.

outline.heading: The Day He gathers them all
outline.gist: Being human is the only condition for being brought to the gathering.

outline.heading: Was it you they worshipped?
outline.gist: Allah asks the angels, the strongest creation, and they answer that He alone is exalted.

outline.heading: The meaning of wali
outline.gist: A wali is the one who has your back and on whom you base your courage.

outline.heading: The wali in marriage
outline.gist: A bride's guardian shows the groom she has a family behind her; among respected Arab families wife-beating could start long wars.

outline.heading: The angels panic though innocent
outline.gist: They never asked to be worshipped, yet the question alarms them.

outline.heading: Isa questioned in the same way
outline.gist: Isa is asked whether he told people to worship him and his mother; the message is for anyone who is followed.

outline.heading: Jinn as the symbol of superstition
outline.gist: People were really following the unseen and superstitious, not the angels.

outline.heading: Notice when you are followed blindly
outline.gist: The angels cannot sin, but anyone followed must be aware of their influence and debunk it.

outline.heading: The Prophet changing plans so he would not be followed blindly
outline.gist: He often took others' suggestions so his personal opinion would not be treated as revelation.

outline.heading: Khalid ibn al-Walid becomes a myth
outline.gist: At Yarmouk an enemy commander asked about Khalid's magic sword; Umar removed him from command so people would not see him as more than human.

outline.heading: No one is beyond human
outline.gist: Never let anyone become more than human in your mind, and never let yourself become that in others' minds.

outline.heading: Neither can benefit nor harm the other
outline.gist: On that Day the improper bond between follower and followed is cut and each carries his own burden.

outline.heading: The Prophet weeping all night over Isa's answer
outline.gist: Even being questioned about what one did not cause is heavy; indirect consequences matter.

outline.heading: Pollinating the palms: I am only human
outline.gist: His passing doubt about pollination ruined a harvest; he taught that only what he conveys from Allah is binding.

outline.heading: A higher level of accountability
outline.gist: Do not accept being followed without question, and speak up when you see something going wrong.

outline.heading: Oppressing yourself by submitting to other than Allah
outline.gist: The soul was created to submit only to Allah; anything less wrongs it.

outline.heading: Recitation of verses 43 to 45
outline.gist: He recites the verses on how the signs were received.

outline.heading: Clear signs and the three answers
outline.gist: When a message challenges the status quo, societies give three standard replies.

outline.heading: First: he wants to turn you from your forefathers' ways
outline.gist: Newness alone is treated as proof of evil, as immigrants' food and dress are resented.

outline.heading: Holding tradition honestly
outline.gist: Keep the good and drop the bad, or the next generation throws it all away; scholars of the past were human.

outline.heading: Second: an invented lie
outline.gist: Ifk means a lie with no basis, the word used for the slander against Aishah; opponents attack credibility.

outline.heading: Third: plain magic
outline.gist: What cannot be explained is branded superstition or bad luck.

outline.heading: The same three cannonballs at every reformer
outline.gist: These replies are not grounds for rejection; the community needs fresh ideas and their bearers must expect the same pushback.

outline.heading: No book before and a warning from earlier nations
outline.gist: The Arabs had no prior scripture to cite, and earlier, stronger nations who rejected their prophets were destroyed.

33:49.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نَكَحۡتُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ ثُمَّ طَلَّقۡتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ فَمَا لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِنَّ مِنۡ عِدَّةࣲ تَعۡتَدُّونَهَاۖ فَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ وَسَرِّحُوهُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:49.en: O ye who believe! If ye wed believing women and divorce them before ye have touched them, then there is no period that ye should reckon. But content them and release them handsomely

33:50.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِنَّآ أَحۡلَلۡنَا لَكَ أَزۡوَٰجَكَ ٱلَّٰتِيٓ ءَاتَيۡتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ يَمِينُكَ مِمَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمِّكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمَّٰتِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَٰلَٰتِكَ ٱلَّٰتِي هَاجَرۡنَ مَعَكَ وَٱمۡرَأَةࣰ مُّؤۡمِنَةً إِن وَهَبَتۡ نَفۡسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنۡ أَرَادَ ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَن يَسۡتَنكِحَهَا خَالِصَةࣰ لَّكَ مِن دُونِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَۗ قَدۡ عَلِمۡنَا مَا فَرَضۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِهِمۡ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ لِكَيۡلَا يَكُونَ عَلَيۡكَ حَرَجࣱۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
33:50.en: O Prophet! Lo! We have made lawful unto thee thy wives unto whom thou hast paid their dowries, and those whom thy right hand possesseth of those whom Allah hath given thee as spoils of war, and the daughters of thine uncle on the father's side and the daughters of thine aunts on the father's side, and the daughters of thine uncle on the mother's side and the daughters of thine aunts on the mother's side who emigrated with thee, and a believing woman if she give herself unto the Prophet and the Prophet desire to ask her in marriage - a privilege for thee only, not for the (rest of) believers - We are Aware of that which We enjoined upon them concerning their wives and those whom their right hands possess - that thou mayst be free from blame, for Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

33:6.ar: ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَوۡلَىٰ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ مِنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡۖ وَأَزۡوَٰجُهُۥٓ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡۗ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ بَعۡضُهُمۡ أَوۡلَىٰ بِبَعۡضࣲ فِي كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ إِلَّآ أَن تَفۡعَلُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَوۡلِيَآئِكُم مَّعۡرُوفࣰ اۚ كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَسۡطُورࣰ ا
33:6.en: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their selves, and his wives are (as) their mothers. And the owners of kinship are closer one to another in the ordinance of Allah than (other) believers and the fugitives (who fled from Mecca), except that ye should do kindness to your friends. This is written in the Book (of nature)

2:282.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيۡنٍ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ى فَٱكۡتُبُوهُۚ وَلۡيَكۡتُب بَّيۡنَكُمۡ كَاتِبُۢ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِۚ وَلَا يَأۡبَ كَاتِبٌ أَن يَكۡتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُۚ فَلۡيَكۡتُبۡ وَلۡيُمۡلِلِ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَلۡيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ وَلَا يَبۡخَسۡ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ فَإِن كَانَ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوۡ ضَعِيفًا أَوۡ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلۡيُمۡلِلۡ وَلِيُّهُۥ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِۚ وَٱسۡتَشۡهِدُواْ شَهِيدَيۡنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمۡۖ فَإِن لَّمۡ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيۡنِ فَرَجُلࣱ وَٱمۡرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرۡضَوۡنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ أَن تَضِلَّ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا ٱلۡأُخۡرَىٰۚ وَلَا يَأۡبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُواْۚ وَلَا تَسۡـَٔمُوٓاْ أَن تَكۡتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوۡ كَبِيرًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَقۡسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقۡوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدۡنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرۡتَابُوٓاْ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةࣰ تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيۡنَكُمۡ فَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكۡتُبُوهَاۗ وَأَشۡهِدُوٓاْ إِذَا تَبَايَعۡتُمۡۚ وَلَا يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبࣱ وَلَا شَهِيدࣱۚ وَإِن تَفۡعَلُواْ فَإِنَّهُۥ فُسُوقُۢ بِكُمۡۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:282.en: O ye who believe! When ye contract a debt for a fixed term, record it in writing. Let a scribe record it in writing between you in (terms of) equity. No scribe should refuse to write as Allah hath taught him, so let him write, and let him who incurreth the debt dictate, and let him observe his duty to Allah his Lord, and diminish naught thereof. But if he who oweth the debt is of low understanding, or weak, or unable himself to dictate, then let the guardian of his interests dictate in (terms of) equity. And call to witness, from among your men, two witnesses. And if two men be not (at hand) then a man and two women, of such as ye approve as witnesses, so that if the one erreth (through forgetfulness) the other will remember. And the witnesses must not refuse when they are summoned. Be not averse to writing down (the contract) whether it be small or great, with (record of) the term thereof. That is more equitable in the sight of Allah and more sure for testimony, and the best way of avoiding doubt between you; save only in the case when it is actual merchandise which ye transfer among yourselves from hand to hand. In that case it is no sin for you if ye write it not. And have witnesses when ye sell one to another, and let no harm be done to scribe or witness. If ye do (harm to them) lo! it is a sin in you. Observe your duty to Allah. Allah is teaching you. And Allah is knower of all things

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

33:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيۡنَ أُمَتِّعۡكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحۡكُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:28.en: O Prophet! Say unto thy wives: If ye desire the world's life and its adornment, come! I will content you and will release you with a fair release

8:63.ar: وَأَلَّفَ بَيۡنَ قُلُوبِهِمۡۚ لَوۡ أَنفَقۡتَ مَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا مَّآ أَلَّفۡتَ بَيۡنَ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَلَّفَ بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
8:63.en: And (as for the believers) hath attuned their hearts. If thou hadst spent all that is in the earth thou couldst not have attuned their hearts, but Allah hath attuned them. Lo! He is Mighty, Wise

CYlmr4hgeXw.speaker_note: Session 16 of his own Sunday Al-Ahzab series; one voice, continues the previous week's verses and aphorism.
CYlmr4hgeXw.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ahzab, Session 16: Divorce Before Consummation and the Prophet's Marriages (33:49-50)
CYlmr4hgeXw.one_line: Rulings specific to the Prophet, why he married several women, the dowry owed to a wife, and the balance between means and devotion.
CYlmr4hgeXw.summary: He opens a new chapter: rulings that applied to the Prophet differently from everyone else. Some bound him more, such as obligatory night prayer, never taking charity and avoiding garlic; others were permissions, chief among them marrying beyond four. He stresses that the Prophet was married to Khadijah alone for twenty-five years and longed for her until his death. His later marriages formed alliances, united feuding tribes, honoured widows and older women, and created the Mothers of the Believers, whose religious standing made Aisha and others leading scholars. In 33:49 a wife divorced before consummation owes no waiting period and is owed half the dowry. He insists the deferred dowry is a debt to be paid whenever a husband can, not only at divorce, that extracting her forgiveness through shame is forbidden, and that inflated dowries do not protect a daughter; character does. 33:50 lists what was permitted to the Prophet, including marrying off women who offered themselves to him, a privilege for him alone that he never used for himself, so that he would feel no distress. He ends with Ibn Ata'illah's second aphorism: work through means when Allah places you there, worship when He calls you to it, and do not flee from one into the other.

outline.heading: Recap: obedience when it is hard
outline.gist: Al-Ahzab's angle on submission is obeying when circumstances are physically, financially or socially hard, so every topic in it is uncomfortable.

outline.heading: Recap: the Trench, the wives, women in the deen
outline.gist: The first three chapters of the surah in brief.

outline.heading: Recap: Zaynab and the Prophet's distress
outline.gist: The command to marry Zaynab and the repeated word haraj, distress.

outline.heading: Recap: dhikr in practice and in words
outline.gist: Asking at every fork in the road what Allah wants, and repeating His praise until it reshapes how you see Him.

outline.heading: Building up a daily wird
outline.gist: Keep the 300 morning and 300 evening phrases until easy, then add more until what seemed impossible becomes normal.

outline.heading: Recap: his five descriptions and status
outline.gist: The verses on his status sit between stories of his private life so no one doubts him.

outline.heading: Rulings that bound him more than us
outline.gist: Night prayer was obligatory on him, he and his family took no charity, and he never ate garlic or onion because he spoke with angels.

outline.heading: A permission given only to him
outline.gist: Others are limited in the number of wives; he was not, and should feel no distress at a ruling that differs from everyone else's.

outline.heading: Married to Khadijah alone for twenty-five years
outline.gist: They had and lost children together; she was only a few years older than him, and he named her among the women who reached perfection.

outline.heading: Remembering Khadijah
outline.gist: Years later he still spoke of her with tears and once halted an army to sit for an hour with her elderly friends to recall her days.

outline.heading: Marriage as alliance
outline.gist: In Arabia, as among European royal families, marriage created political alliances between tribes.

outline.heading: Marrying the daughters of his enemies
outline.gist: Safiyyah, daughter of a fierce Jewish opponent, and Umm Habibah, daughter of Abu Sufyan, showed that no one carries another's guilt.

outline.heading: Women of remarkable lives
outline.gist: Umm Salamah endured a year separated from husband and child and migrated alone; each wife was a person of great stature.

outline.heading: Mothers of the Believers: a religious status
outline.gist: Their title gave them authority and protection after his death; caliphs could not transgress against them, and Hafsah kept the compiled Quran.

outline.heading: Aisha's narrations and the testimony question
outline.gist: Aisha is among the top narrators and much fiqh rests on her word alone, which answers misconceptions drawn from the verse on two female witnesses.

outline.heading: No distress about his marriages
outline.gist: Muslims asked about the Prophet's wives should feel no awkwardness, because 33:36 applies; the coming verses enter his home.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:49 and counting the ghunnah
outline.gist: He recites the verse, teaching two counts on each nasal sound, even when stopping on it.

outline.heading: Divorce before consummation: no waiting period
outline.gist: If a marriage contract is signed and the couple separate before intimacy, the woman owes no iddah of three cycles.

outline.heading: The deferred dowry is a debt
outline.gist: The later portion of the mahr is owed as soon as the husband can pay, and on his death it is paid before inheritance is divided; gifts do not count.

outline.heading: Do not ask her to forgive it
outline.gist: Taking her right by pressing her shame or embarrassment is forbidden; pay it first, and what she returns of her own will is hers to give.

outline.heading: Half the dowry, and a contract worth a fortune
outline.gist: Divorce before consummation means paying half the mahr; a contract he witnessed in gold coins came to a debt of about 150,000 dollars.

outline.heading: Inflated dowries do not protect a daughter
outline.gist: A wife is protected by a husband's character, values and respect, not by a sum he resents and can never earn.

outline.heading: Release them beautifully
outline.gist: The third call in the surah for a graceful divorce, especially needed when a contract ends before the wedding and people start questioning the woman.

outline.heading: Recitation of 33:50
outline.gist: He begins reciting the verse specific to the Prophet.

outline.heading: Wives given their dowry, and those not free
outline.gist: Allah made lawful his wives whose dowry he paid on the spot and those who were not free.

outline.heading: He married widows and older women
outline.gist: Sawdah, the first Muslim widow, was elderly; Umm Habibah and others were in their fifties.

outline.heading: "Daughters of your uncles and aunts"
outline.gist: This means women of Arabia distantly related through either parent, as people still say cousin of anyone traceable; Zaynab was his only actual cousin.

outline.heading: Each marriage brought a tribe to Islam
outline.gist: His wives came from different key tribes, and a study traces tribes migrating to Madinah months after each marriage.

outline.heading: Uniting people who hated one another
outline.gist: Centuries of tribal hatred, like divisions today between countries, regions and villages, were overcome as Allah joined hearts.

outline.heading: A woman who offers herself: marrying her off
outline.gist: Yastankihaha means to give her in marriage to someone, not to marry her himself, a point many commentators missed.

outline.heading: The woman married for the Quran he knew
outline.gist: A woman offered herself; he married her to a companion who owned not even an iron ring, with the surahs he knew as her dowry.

outline.heading: "Exclusively for you"
outline.gist: No one after him may marry a woman off without a dowry on her offering herself; he never took any such woman for himself.

outline.heading: The burden of his fame
outline.gist: Everyone wanted a piece of him; women sought famous men because a wife gained status that helped her family, so such offers were common.

outline.heading: Permitted, yet he did not take it
outline.gist: Even what was made lawful for him he declined, which shows he sought nothing for himself; the rulings served unity and honoured women.

outline.heading: How we know a ruling was his alone
outline.gist: Specificity is known when the Quran says so explicitly, as here; it ends with his death.

outline.heading: So there is no distress upon you
outline.gist: Allah knows what He prescribed for other believers; this exception exists to remove distress from the Prophet, and in its time and place it was normal.

outline.heading: How the marriages eased his task
outline.gist: Most came in his last years as the state formed; Safiyyah, once Jewish, and Mariyah, once Christian, joined the Abrahamic faiths in his household.

outline.heading: Ibn Ata'illah's second aphorism, restated
outline.gist: Wanting devotion where Allah placed you in means is a hidden desire; wanting means where He placed you in devotion is a fall from a higher rank.

outline.heading: Tajrid and asbab: the unseen and the seen
outline.gist: Muslims live between a world of observable causes and a world beyond them, and must follow the rules of whichever they are in.

outline.heading: Expecting success without effort
outline.gist: Asking Allah for results He made attainable only through study and work is running away from the station He set.

outline.heading: When a trial has no logical cause
outline.gist: A healthy non-smoker struck by lung disease should treat it as a test from beyond the rules, not torment himself over what he did wrong.

outline.heading: Work in the time for work, pray in the time for prayer
outline.gist: Skipping work to make dua is a hidden desire; skipping congregation for work is a fall from the rank Allah gave you.

hadith.gist: Whoever eats garlic or onion should not come near the mosque; the Prophet avoided them because he conversed with those others do not.
Many men reached perfection but among women only a few, Khadijah among them; the best of the women of her time was Khadijah.

A woman offered herself to the Prophet; he married her to a man who had not even an iron ring, with the Quran he knew as her dowry.

takeaways: Pay your wife's deferred dowry as soon as you can; do not wait for divorce or death.
Never pressure a wife into forgiving her dowry.
